definition: The card issuer's cardholder authentication (strong customer authentication) that Stripe.js runs inside `confirmPayment` on the storefront's card step when the card requires it. After the challenge Stripe returns the browser to `/checkout/complete.html?id=…`, which turns the authorised payment into a booking. Stripe test card `4000 0027 6000 3184` always asks for it.

A person's login on the platform (`platform.accounts`, id `acc_…`): e-mail, Argon2id password, optional TOTP MFA, `is_platform_admin` and a status (`pending_verification` until the address is verified, then `active`; `disabled` blocks sign-in; the CHECK also lists `locked`, which is never set because lockout uses `locked_until`, and `deleted`). OTA owners, their staff and Velexis staff are all accounts, and one account can belong to several OTAs through [[membership]] rows.

Brute-force protection on password sign-in. On the platform the fifth consecutive wrong password sets `platform.accounts.locked_until` 15 minutes ahead and answers `423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED` with `Retry-After`; a platform admin can clear it with Unlock on `/accounts/<id>` (audited as `account.unlocked`). For storefront customers five wrong sign-ins for one e-mail within 15 minutes lock that address for 15 minutes through the Redis counter `t:<tenantId>:<env>:authfail:<sha256(email)>`, which also counts unknown addresses so the answers never reveal which e-mails have an account.

The storefront header slot for the session: visitors see 'Sign in' (with `next` back to the current page), signed-in customers see 'Hi, <first name>', My account and Sign out. Below 1024 px (`lg`) these collapse into one 'Account' disclosure button; from 1024 px they sit in the navigation row with the greeting capped at 12rem.

Which Stripe account takes an OTA's traveller payments, stored in `platform.payment_provider_connections.account_mode`: `velexis` (the default; Velexis's own account collects and pays the OTA through monthly [[settlement]]s), `connect_standard` (the OTA's own account linked by Connect OAuth and called with the `Stripe-Account` header) or `api_keys` (the OTA's own Stripe keys, verified as a credential submission).

The idempotency key of an OTA admin form or confirmation dialog: rendered once with the page in the hidden field `actionKey`, it reaches the API as the SDK's `idempotencyKey` (`Idempotency-Key` header). After a final `4xx` the API stored, the action state carries a fresh `nextActionKey` so the next submit is a new request. After `412`, `429`, a `5xx`, a timeout, `409 CONFLICT` (`idempotency_key_in_use`) or `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` (whose message asks for a reload) the same key is sent again, so a retry replays or waits for the first request.

The rule (ADR-0023) that every `uses:` in `.github/workflows/` and `.github/actions/` names a full 40-character commit SHA with its tag in a comment, so Dependabot can bump both; `tools/ci/check-package-json.mjs` fails on any other form.

The platform admin console's home page (`/`): OTAs by status, provisioning failures of the last 24 hours, failed jobs per platform queue, office-pool levels, open live-office requests and the M5 'To review' counters, each linking to its filtered list. It is one `adminGetDashboard` call.

The platform CLI's admin bootstrap commands, run by the developer (on the VM: `sudo velexis-run platform node dist/cli.js admin:grant <email> --operator <name>`). `admin:grant` makes an `active`, e-mail-verified account with MFA a platform admin, and `admin:reset-mfa` is the emergency MFA reset of a platform admin; no migration or production seed creates an admin. Both write audit rows with `actor_type = 'system'`.

`platform/admin/src/middleware.ts`, run before every page, server action and route handler of the platform admin: deny by default (only `/sign-in`, `/sign-in/mfa` and `/sign-out` are public; everything else redirects to `/sign-in` with a safe `next`), a single-flight `adminRefresh` when the access token expires within 30 s, and a per-request nonce CSP plus `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`.

A platform admin's signed-in session in the console: a 15-minute access JWT with audience `platform_admin` and a rotating refresh token (2 idle hours, at most the family's 12 hours), kept in the `__Host-vxa_at` / `__Host-vxa_rt` cookies (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict). A portal session never opens the console and an admin session never opens the portal.

The file encryption tool `age`, used for the nightly backups and the shipped security logs: files are encrypted to public keys whose private halves stay offline, and the `/etc/velexis` configuration goes to a separate config key, so no single stolen set holds both the data and the keys to it.

The file-integrity checker run daily by Ubuntu's `dailyaidecheck.timer` against `/var/lib/aide/aide.db` (PCI DSS 11.5.2). `velexis-logreview` reviews its reports and alerts on changes, errors or a stale run, and `auditd` watches the baseline itself (key `velexis-aide`).

Re-initialising AIDE's database after intended changes. `provision-vm.sh` runs `aideinit` once, at the end of the first run in which every step completed, and records it in `/var/lib/velexis/provision/aide-rebaseline`; later re-baselines are manual and recorded as `manual` lines, which `check-vm.sh` compares with the database's SHA-256.

The payment method in which the traveller's card goes, in memory only, from the storefront's isolated card page through the OTA API to Amadeus Flight Create Orders as a `CREDIT_CARD` form of payment, and the airline charges it: no Stripe, and the checkout switches to `pricing_mode = net` (the airline's price, no OTA markup or fees). It needs `AIRLINE_CARD_ENABLED=true` (off in production until the go-live runbook is signed off) and the OTA's `airline_card_enabled_test` / `_live` setting; only [[edge-caller]]s may send it (`checkout.completeWithAirlineCard`), at most 3 attempts per checkout, only brand, BIN and last 4 are stored, and the OTA admin never takes card data (refunds go `refund_via_airline`).

The `allowUnpaid` option of the OTA admin's issue-tickets dialog, shown only to owners and admins, that issues a booking whose payment is not captured, for example an airline-card booking the airline has not charged. Other roles are told to capture the payment first or cancel.

The flags `bookings.get` returns (`allowedActions`: `canCancel`, `canModifyContacts`, …) that decide which self-service controls the storefront's booking page shows (change contacts, cancel, refresh, download documents) and why an action is refused: `flown`, `too_close_to_departure` (3 hours or less before the first departure), `disabled_by_ota` or `pending`. [[cancellation-mode]] uses the same rule.

Velexis's only flight supplier: 12 Enterprise operations (offers search, branded fares upsell, offers price, create orders, order issue, order management, retrieve by record locator, queue list, …) plus the OAuth token endpoint, typed from the specifications in `docs/amadeus-api/`. Only the OTA backend's `AmadeusClient` calls flight operations; the platform worker only requests tokens to verify credentials.

A 9-character Amadeus office id (the PCC, e.g. `DEV1A0001`) on whose behalf orders are created, queued and ticketed; its owner and queuing office decide which orders an OTA may see ([[office-isolation]]). Velexis's pool lives in `platform.amadeus_offices` with status `available`, `assigned` (to one OTA's `velexis` connection), `releasing` (after that OTA moved to its own credentials) or `retired`.

`tools/amadeus-stub` (`pnpm stub:amadeus`), a local Node HTTP double of Amadeus Enterprise on `127.0.0.1:4900` for development, tests and e2e: the OAuth token endpoint and the 12 operations validated against the Amadeus specifications, recorded fixtures, and scenarios chosen per request with `X-Stub-Scenario` (`sold-out`, `price-changed`, `ticketing-failed`, `server-error`, `timeout`, …), which the OTA API forwards outside production. Destination `ZZZ` returns no offers and card `4000000000000002` is declined; the stub never runs on the VM and refuses to start in production.

The OTA backend's Redis cache of Amadeus OAuth tokens: one token per credential set and environment in `amadeus:token:<credId>:<env>`, envelope-encrypted and kept until `expires_in` minus 60 s, refilled under the single-flight lock `amadeus:tokenlock:<credId>:<env>` (`SET NX EX 10`). Every OTA on the Velexis Amadeus account shares the same token.

An OTA's credential for the OTA API, sent as `X-Api-Key`: `<pk|sk>_<test|live>_` plus 40 base62 characters, either [[publishable-key]] (`pk_`, browser-safe, exact allowed origins) or [[secret-key]] (`sk_`, server only, scopes). It is created in the portal and shown once; `platform.api_keys` keeps only the 14-character prefix, `last4` and an HMAC-SHA-256 under the [[api-key-pepper]], with scopes, optional expiry and revocation, and the OTA API records the last use in Redis `apikey:used:<keyId>` (at most once a minute).

The secret key file (32 random bytes, `API_KEY_PEPPER_FILE`) used as the HMAC-SHA-256 key of API key hashes (`hashApiKey` in `@velexis/crypto`). The platform issues keys and the OTA API verifies them, so both backends hold an identical copy, generated once by `provision-vm.sh`; it is never rotated in the MVP.

The error class both backends throw, `new AppError(code, { message?, details?, fieldErrors?, supplier?, cause? })` from `@velexis/errors`: only catalogue codes type-check and the HTTP status comes from the [[error-catalogue]]. `cause` stays in the logs and never reaches the response.

A difference between the SDK and its frozen [[contract-declarations]] that an ADR allows, listed in `ota/sdk/test/contract/deviations.ts` so the contract test accepts it. Today there is only one: the three auth methods whose result is typed `AuthSessionResult | AuthSessionInfo`, because cookie mode returns no tokens (OADR-0006).

The string `<schema>.<table>.<column>:<rowId>` (`aadFor` in `@velexis/crypto`) authenticated with every AES-256-GCM ciphertext of [[envelope-encryption]], so a value copied to another row, column or tenant schema fails to decrypt.

The platform admin's CSV download of filtered audit rows (`/audit/export.csv`, `adminExportAudit`) for a required period of at most one year and at most 100 000 rows, streamed by the console's route handler with `no-store`. Every export is itself audited as `audit.exported`.

The append-only `platform.platform_audit_log`: one row per platform state change, written in the same transaction as the change, with actor type, account and e-mail snapshot, action, target, tenant, request id, IP, user agent and redacted before/after details (including the reason of admin actions). The platform admin searches it on `/audit` with every filter in the URL; the OTA side's equivalent is [[staff-action]].

The Linux audit daemon on the VM, whose rules (installed by `provision-vm.sh`) watch `/etc/velexis` and its keys, `/etc/caddy`, the systemd units, `/usr/local/sbin`, sudoers, sshd and AIDE's baseline, tagged with keys such as `velexis-keys`, `velexis-aide`, `caddy-config` and `caddy-binary`. Its records reach the journal and the shipped security logs.

A console read of the OTA API marked with the `@AuditedRead` decorator that writes a `staff_actions` row because it returns one person's data or a supplier record: `customer.view`, `pnr.lookup`, `order.retrieve` and the raw `amadeus.*` reads.

The SDK's handling of `401 TOKEN_EXPIRED`: it refreshes once (cookie mode: `POST /v1/auth/refresh` with the refresh cookie; token and server mode: with the refresh token and the API key only) and resends the original call once with the same idempotency key. A refused refresh calls `onSessionExpired` and throws its `AuthenticationError`.

What `velexis-deploy` does when a unit does not answer `/health/ready` within `HEALTH_TIMEOUT` (90 s per unit by default) after a deploy's restart: it re-installs the previous release's units and Caddyfile from its snapshot, points `current` back at it, restarts and exits 1. `sudo velexis-deploy --rollback` does the same by hand; migrations are never reversed (see [[expand-and-contract]]).

One night's backup written by `deploy/scripts/backup.sh` (`velexis-backup`): `velexis-db.dump.age`, `globals.sql.age`, `storage.tar.zst.age`, `redis-aof.tar.zst.age`, `config.tar.zst.age` (with AIDE's baseline) and `MANIFEST.txt`, uploaded immutable to `daily/<date>/` of the off-site bucket (and `monthly/` on the 1st). The recovery point objective is up to 24 hours.

The `beforeCommit` callback of `migrateTenantSchema` (`@velexis/db`), run inside the provisioning transaction after the tenant migration files, so an OTA's seed rows commit together with its new schema. It must not BEGIN or COMMIT, and a throw rolls back the schema too.

Backend-for-frontend: the portal, the platform admin and the OTA admin are Next.js servers whose server components and server actions are the only callers of the API for their UI, using tokens kept in HttpOnly cookies, so no API token reaches browser JavaScript (ADR-0014). The portal and platform admin call the platform API on loopback with the [[bff-key]] and forward the visitor in [[end-user-headers]]; the OTA admin uses the SDK server side with its service key.

The shared secret `PLATFORM_BFF_KEY` (at least 32 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) that the portal and the platform admin send as `X-Velexis-Bff-Key`. Only a loopback request carrying it may set the [[end-user-headers]], which the platform API then uses for rate limits, sessions and audit rows (PADR-0019); it is configuration and never logged.

`platform.tenants.billing_notice` (`past_due` or `trial_ending`, NULL for none). Billing sync sets `past_due` from a `past_due` or `paused` Stripe subscription, and the daily `billing.manual_trials` schedule sets `trial_ending` and then `past_due` for a manual trial. It drives the billing banner of the portal and of the OTA admin shell (reported by `console.auth.me` for every role), where owners and finance staff get a link to the portal's billing page.

An order of an OTA in `tenant_<key>.bookings` (id `bkg_…`), created from a completed checkout: status `pending`, `confirmed`, `ticketed`, `partially_ticketed`, `cancelled` or `failed`, a separate `ticketing_status`, money columns, the Velexis [[booking-reference]], the airline [[record-locator]] and the Amadeus order snapshot.
A PDF the OTA worker renders per booking version (`booking_documents`): the itinerary and one e-ticket receipt per ticket. It is downloaded through a 5-minute [[signed-url]].

The Velexis reference a traveller reads in every booking e-mail and types with a last name in the [[guest-lookup]]: `VX` plus 6 characters from an alphabet without look-alikes (no I, O, 0 or 1), e.g. `VX7K2M9Q`, unique per tenant in `bookings.reference` (whose CHECK accepts 6 to 10 capitals and digits). It is also written into the Amadeus order as the remark `VELEXIS <reference>` and differs from the airline's [[record-locator]].

What the airline needs for a fare (e-mail, mobile phone, dates of birth, passport or ID details, addresses), returned with the [[priced-offer]] as `bookingRequirements`. The storefront's checkout builds its traveller and contact fields from it.

The OTA worker's periodic re-read of live bookings from Amadeus Flight Order Management (`bookings.sync_scan`, then one `booking.sync` per booking): a booking is due when last synced 6 hours ago or more, or 1 hour when it still waits for tickets within 24 hours of its ticketing deadline, oldest first. It records schedule changes, issued tickets and airline cancellations.

The Amadeus Branded Fares Upsell call for one offer (`flights.upsell`), behind the storefront offer page's fare cards when `features.brandedFareUpsell` is on. The airline's [[fare-family]] alternatives are stored as new `flight_offers` rows with `origin = 'upsell'`, and an identical request reuses the stored answer (`offer_upsells`).

The Redis-backed job queue library both backends use: every key carries the prefix `vx` (`vx:<queue>:…`), each queue has one consuming worker, and jobs default to 5 attempts with exponential backoff from 30 s, failed jobs kept 30 days and completed ones 1 day. Queue names are defined once in `@velexis/api-types/jobs`; the platform admin can retry failed jobs of platform queues only.

The web server at the edge of the single VM (`deploy/caddy/Caddyfile`): TLS for every public host (on demand for storefront sub-domains and verified custom domains), reverse proxy to the apps on 127.0.0.1, the storefront's static `dist/` files (with `/p/*` served by `p.html`), edge headers on storefront `/api/*`, security headers and CSP, the Coraza WAF, request ids, the maintenance page and filtered access logs. Locally the Vite [[dev-proxy]] plays its storefront role.

Caddy's admin API, bound only to the unix socket `/run/caddy/admin.sock` in a 0700 directory owned by the `caddy` user and never to TCP port 2019, so no app process can replace the live configuration.

The systemd drop-in `deploy/systemd/caddy.service.d/velexis.conf`: it loads `caddy.env`, creates `/run/caddy` and starts Caddy without `--environ` (which would print the edge secret). A drop-in applies only when Caddy starts, so a deploy restarts Caddy when the installed drop-in differs from the hash recorded in `/var/lib/velexis/caddy-dropin.sha256`.

What cancelling a booking now would do, decided in `cancellation-mode.ts` (first match wins): `not_allowed` (`canCancel` is false: cancelled, flown, 3 hours or less before departure, disabled by the OTA, or not live), `release` (nothing ticketed: the order is deleted and the authorisation voided or the payment refunded), `void` (every ticket was issued today in the OTA's time zone) or `request_only` (anything else: staff handle it with the airline). The contract's enum also has `refund`, which the MVP never returns because it has no automatic airline refund. The storefront's cancel dialog and the OTA admin show the mode and refund estimate before confirming.

The fee for the chosen card brand (and BIN): the Amadeus credit-card fee, re-quoted with Flight Offers Price when the payment's card hint changes, plus any OTA `payment_card` [[fee-rule]]. It is stored on the payment with its lines (`payments.card_fee_lines`, which record whether a cancellation refunds each), and the review step shows the final total including it.

How the SDK's `checkout.completeWithAirlineCard` rebuilds any error it throws: card-named fields are removed from `details` and `supplier`, the card number (and its last 12 digits), security code and holder name are replaced by `[redacted]` in every text and number, and a `cause` that holds any of them is dropped, so no card data can reach page logs.

The PCI DSS cardholder data environment. Because nothing on the single VM is segmented, the whole VM is the CDE (ADR-0027), while GitHub Actions, the SSH path, the off-site bucket and the provider accounts are connected systems in scope.

The final status `carried_forward` of an approved settlement whose net is zero or negative: nothing is paid and the balance moves to a later statement (`platform.settlements.carried_to_id`), enforced by the CHECK `settlements_carry_ck`.

The CI check `tools/ci/check-no-hardcoded-hosts.mjs` that fails on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `:5432` or `:6379` in the code of `platform/*/src`, `ota/*/src`, `packages/*/src` and `tools/reference-data/src` (comments and a reviewed allow-list aside), so moving to managed PostgreSQL or Redis stays a configuration change.

The CI check `tools/ci/check-package-json.mjs` that fails on a dependency that is not an exact version (or `workspace:*`), on `@velexis/testing` or `@velexis/amadeus-stub` outside devDependencies, on a package under `packages/` that depends on an app, and on a GitHub Action not pinned to a full commit SHA with its tag in a comment.

`deploy/scripts/check-vm.sh`, a read-only verifier of the VM's hardening that prints one PASS or FAIL per item in groups (system, services, audit, firewall, ssh, database, redis, caddy, users, files, envfiles) and never prints a secret value. Its tests run in CI's `check-vm` job.

The server-side record of one purchase attempt (`tenant_<key>.checkouts`, id `chk_…`, with `checkout_*` child rows) opened from a [[priced-offer]]: travellers (documents encrypted), contacts, extras, remarks and payment, a `version` for If-Match and an expiry from `checkout_ttl_minutes`. Its status is `open`, `payment_pending`, `completed`, `expired` or `abandoned`, and it leads to at most one [[booking]].

A Stripe-hosted Checkout page that the platform API creates (`createCheckoutSession`) for an OTA owner's plan subscription. The portal redirects only to the absolute https `checkoutUrl` the API answered, and Stripe's webhook, not the redirect, confirms the payment. Not to be confused with the traveller [[checkout]].

One of the four steps of the storefront's `/checkout.html` (Travellers, Contact details, Extras, Payment), each a browser history entry. A step opens only when the steps before it are complete, and every save sends `If-Match` with the checkout version shown on screen.

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, run on every pull request and push to `main`, with the jobs `plan-lint`, `deploy-files`, `systemd-units`, `check-vm`, `dev-setup`, `build-test`, `integration`, `alt-hosts` and `sdk-node22` (the last not required).

The SDK client made by `createVelexisClient` plus every client derived from it with `withOptions`. They share one refresh per refresh-token value (token and server mode) or one cookie refresh state (cookie mode), so no refresh token is presented twice; two separate `createVelexisClient` calls, or two browser tabs, share nothing except, in cookie mode, the origin's Web Lock `velexis-sdk:cookie-refresh`, which makes their cookie refreshes run one at a time.

The OTA admin's shared dialog for consequential actions (`ConfirmDialog`): a summary of the effect, the environment badge with a LIVE warning, a reason of 3 to 500 characters (none where the contract takes none) and the hidden [[action-key]] and version.

A secret API key with the key scope `console:automation` plus permission scopes (for example `amadeus:read`) that lets an OTA's own server call `/v1/console/**`: key-only calls are limited to those permissions, while with a staff token the staff member's role decides. `dev:seed` creates one for the demo OTA (development only).

The `/v1/console/**` operations of the OTA API, exposed as the SDK's `console.*` methods, for OTA staff and console automation keys. Every call checks a staff permission and the environment, and changes and refusals are written to `staff_actions`; who may reach them is described under [[console-scope]].

The portal page `/console?tenant=<id>` that lists the account's OTAs with an Open console button each, starting the [[sso]] hand-off into the OTA admin; the OTA admin sends people without a session there.

The caller class of the `/v1/console/**` operations, in which net amounts, markups and supplier details are visible and every call is checked against a staff permission and audited. It is reached by the OTA admin's [[service-key]], by a secret key not scoped `storefront` together with a staff token, or by a [[console-automation-key]].

An OTA's own storefront page (terms, privacy, FAQ, about …) in `storefront_pages`, written in a Markdown subset in the OTA admin and published per locale. The storefront serves it at `/p/<slug>` through `p.html`, building it from parsed blocks with `createElement` only, and lists pages with `show_in_footer` in the footer.

The storefront's CSP response header, set by Caddy: `default-src 'self'`, scripts only from self and Stripe, `style-src 'self'`, `frame-ancestors 'none'` and `worker-src 'none'`, with stricter headers on the airline-card page. The build has no inline script or style, and `vite preview` sends a copy that `ota/frontend/test/csp.test.js` compares with the Caddyfile; the portal and platform admin use a per-request [[csp-nonce]] instead.

The frozen TypeScript declarations of the SDK's public API in `docs/velexis-sdk/sdk/src/*.d.ts` (`index`, `shared`, `identity`, `flights`, `bookings`, `console`). They are never edited: the SDK may add but never remove or narrow, and additions are recorded in the OpenAPI document and `extensions.md`.

The SDK's `tsc` project under `ota/sdk/test/contract` that compiles declarations emitted from `src/` against the [[contract-declarations]], with generated per-method assignability checks, hand-written client checks, the [[approved-deviation]] list, the runtime [[parity-test]] and the `@throws` test.

The contract-first commands: `pnpm contracts:lint` lints both OpenAPI documents with Redocly, and `pnpm contracts:generate` regenerates the API types, the operations index and the error catalogue. CI runs the generation again and fails when the committed files differ.

The storefront theme rule (`CONTRAST_RULES` in `lib/theme.js`) that switches the whole palette to the neutral one when any OTA colour is invalid or any text pair is below WCAG 4.5:1, so brand and neutral colours never mix; fonts and corner radius still apply.

The platform side of Velexis, which manages OTAs as Velexis's customers: accounts, tenants, plans and billing, supplier and payment connections, domains, API keys and staff operations. It is the platform API with its worker, used through the portal and the platform admin; it never serves travellers (the OTA backend does) and never touches tenant schemas.

The SDK session mode of the hosted storefront (`session: 'cookie'`): same-origin `fetch` to `/api` with the HttpOnly session cookies the API sets, `X-CSRF-Token` on writes and one automatic cookie refresh on `401 TOKEN_EXPIRED`, run under the origin's Web Lock `velexis-sdk:cookie-refresh` where the browser has Web Locks, so two tabs never refresh at once. Every key and token is refused with a `TypeError`, so no credential reaches page JavaScript.

The Coraza web application firewall with the OWASP Core Rule Set, compiled into Caddy (PCI DSS 6.4.2). It blocks on the OTA API host (`api.ota.example.com`) and on storefront `/api/*` and `/checkout/*` (mode `VELEXIS_WAF_ENGINE`, default `On`), refusing with `403 FORBIDDEN`, `400` for a body it cannot parse, or `413`; on the portal, admin hosts, platform API and storefront pages it only logs.

An OTA's own Amadeus credentials or Stripe API keys, held envelope-encrypted in `platform.credential_submissions` (id `crs_…`) while the platform worker verifies them: status `pending`, `verifying`, `applied`, `failed` or `superseded`. They are applied only on success, so a typo never breaks a working connection, and the secret is erased once the submission leaves `pending`/`verifying`.

A fresh 128-bit value per request that the portal's (and the platform admin's) middleware puts into the Content-Security-Policy (`script-src 'self' 'nonce-…'`) and hands to Next.js, so only the app's own scripts run; for this reason every page is rendered per request.

The storefront's double-submit token: a 256-bit base64url value in `__Host-vx_csrf`, the only cookie page JavaScript may read, which the SDK copies into `X-CSRF-Token` on every state-changing edge request; the API also requires the storefront's own `Origin` and answers `403 CSRF_TOKEN_INVALID` on a mismatch. The value rotates at sign-in, sign-out and password change, and the SDK fetches it again once (`GET /v1/storefront`) when it is missing or refused.

How list operations page: the API answers `{ data, page: { nextCursor, limit } }`, and the SDK wraps it in a `Page` with `next()` and `for await` over all pages, fetching each page only when the previous one is used up. Extra fields such as `totalCount` stay on the page.

An OTA-owned host (e.g. `travel.acme.example.com`) that serves its hosted storefront next to `<key>.ota.example.com`: a `platform.tenant_domains` row with `kind = 'custom'`, added in the portal when `FEATURE_CUSTOM_DOMAINS` is on and the plan's `customDomains` limit allows. It stays `pending` for up to 72 hours until [[domain-verification]] succeeds, then Caddy serves it with [[on-demand-tls]]; platform admins can re-check or remove one (with a reason) on `/domains`.

A traveller's account at one OTA (`tenant_<key>.customers`, id `cus_…`); the same e-mail at two OTAs is two customers. A signed-in customer holds a [[customer-session]] in the `__Host-vx_at` / `__Host-vx_rt` cookies, and a deleted customer is erased within 30 days by [[customer-erasure]].

The hourly `customers.erase` job (minute 50, fanned out per active or suspended tenant) that permanently erases customers deleted at least 30 days less 1 hour 5 minutes ago, at most 100 per job: identities, sessions and consents go, checkouts, bookings and payments are detached (with a `customer.erased` event) and account e-mails lose their address. `account.delete` itself acts at once: sessions revoked, address replaced, `customers.status = 'deleted'`.

Stripe's hosted Customer Portal (`createCustomerPortalSession`), where an OTA owner changes the card or plan of the Velexis subscription or cancels it; it opens from the portal's Billing page (Manage in Stripe) and returns to it.

A storefront customer's signed-in session at one OTA: a stateless 15-minute EdDSA access JWT in `__Host-vx_at` and a rotating opaque refresh token in `__Host-vx_rt`, stored as its SHA-256 in `customer_sessions` (`refresh_token_hash`, `rotated_at`, `replaced_by_id`, `revoked_at`, `revoke_reason`). The session lasts 12 hours, or 30 days with remember me, and reusing an old refresh token revokes the whole family.

The four PostgreSQL login roles of `deploy/postgres/bootstrap.sql`: `velexis_migrator` (DDL at deploy time; owns the database, `platform` and `reference`), `velexis_provisioner` (owns the tenant schemas), `velexis_platform_app` (DML on `platform` and `reference`) and `velexis_ota_app` (DML on tenant schemas, read-only `reference` and selected platform tables, with `search_path = pg_catalog` so it resolves no schema outside `tenantTx`).

The seeded catch-all markup rule (`markup_rules.is_default`, priority 1000) that matches every offer. It cannot be deleted, narrowed, switched off, dated or re-prioritised: such a change answers `409 CONFLICT` with `details.reason = 'default_rule'`, while its markup amounts can still be edited.

One of the 19 operations of the OTA contract marked `x-milestone: deferred` that the MVP does not build (saved travellers, preferences, data exports, extras after booking, `storefront.resolve`, `flights.availability`, console creates, raw Amadeus writes …). Its route exists and answers `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` with `details.milestone` and `details.operationId`, and the SDK throws a non-retryable `ServerError`.

`defineConfig` from `@velexis/config`, the typed configuration loader: each app declares its environment variables once with `env.*` builders, and validation fails with one `ConfigError` listing every problem by variable name, never by value. It is the only code allowed to read `process.env`.

The OTA with the reserved key `demo` (schema `tenant_demo`). Locally the OTA backend's `dev:seed` creates it as 'Demo Travel' on `demo.ota.example.com` in test mode, with no owner, an Amadeus test connection, a Stripe test connection and three test API keys printed once (development only). In production `tenants:create-demo <owner e-mail>` creates Velexis's own demo OTA with a manual active subscription, kept out of billing and watched by the uptime monitor.

The locked system account `deploy` that GitHub Actions uses over SSH (public key with `restrict`: no TTY, no forwarding). It may only rsync into `/srv/velexis/incoming` and run `sudo /usr/local/sbin/velexis-deploy` (ADR-0023).

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, started by hand only (`workflow_dispatch`): a `build` job without secrets (lint, typecheck, test, build, pack the release), the `e2e` job on the same commit through the E2E workflow, then the `deploy` job in the `production` environment, which uploads the release, runs `velexis-deploy` and smoke-checks `--status`.

The human launch step of X-039: run the WAF with `VELEXIS_WAF_ENGINE=DetectionOnly` in `caddy.env` for at least a week, add exclusions for legitimate matches, then remove the line and reload Caddy so the blocking paths block.

`tools/dev/dev-keys.mjs` (`pnpm dev:keys`), which creates `.local/keys/` (0700) with five 0600 key files (`master-v1.key`, `api-key-pepper`, `document-url.key` and the platform and OTA Ed25519 JWT keys) plus `.local/storage/`. It never overwrites without `--force` and never prints key material.

The storefront's Vite dev server (port 5173) and preview (4173) routing that mimics Caddy for one OTA: `/api/*` goes to `OTA_API_URL` with `/api` stripped and `X-Velexis-Edge`, `X-Velexis-Host` (`STOREFRONT_DEV_HOST`) and `Origin` added; `/p/*` serves `p.html`, unknown paths get the 404 page and internal paths are blocked.

The development-only `dev:seed` CLI commands of both backends, refused in production. The platform's creates the admin `admin@example.com` (random password and TOTP URI printed once), the Velexis test Amadeus account and 40 test offices `DEV1A0001` to `DEV1A0040`; the OTA backend's creates the [[demo-ota]] with three test API keys. The e2e stack runs both and discards their output.

`deploy/scripts/dev-setup.sh`, the one-time local setup of PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 7.4 with the development passwords of `.env.example`: the four [[database-roles]] plus `velexis_test_admin` for the integration tests, and Redis password `dev_redis` (development only). It refuses to run where `/etc/velexis` exists, and CI runs it in the `dev-setup` job.

The currency a traveller picks in the storefront header when the OTA sells in two or more: stored in localStorage `vx.currency`, sent as `X-Currency` through `client.withOptions({ currency })`, and applied to the next search only (nothing reloads).

The DNS proof of a [[custom-domain]]: `TXT _velexis.<host>` holding the row's token plus a CNAME chain to `<key>.<STOREFRONT_BASE_DOMAIN>` (or A/AAAA records pointing at the VM), checked by the platform worker through public resolvers. A `pending` domain is checked every 5 minutes for 72 hours and then becomes `verified` or `failed`; verified domains are re-checked daily and fail at the third consecutive failed re-check.

Playwright's global setup `tools/e2e/support/stack.ts`: it creates a fresh database `velexis_e2e_<runId>`, migrates it and loads reference data, starts the built apps (with `E2E_WITH_OTA=1` also the Amadeus stub, OTA API, OTA worker, OTA admin and three storefront previews), runs both dev seeds, and tears everything down afterwards.

`.github/workflows/e2e.yml`, which runs the Playwright projects (portal, platform-admin, storefront, ota-admin, plus the Stripe projects and SDK smoke tests) nightly at 02:23 UTC, on demand, on pull requests labelled `e2e`, and as a called workflow (`workflow_call`) from Deploy before anything reaches the VM.

The hosted storefront as the OTA API sees it: a request that reached `/api/*` through Caddy (or the Vite dev proxy) carrying the [[edge-secret]] in `X-Velexis-Edge` and the verified storefront host in `X-Velexis-Host`. Only edge callers get cookie sessions with CSRF checks, and only they may submit an [[airline-card]] payment.

`VELEXIS_EDGE_SECRET`, shared by `caddy.env` and `ota-backend.env`: Caddy sends it as `X-Velexis-Edge` (with `X-Velexis-Host`) on storefront `/api/*` requests after removing any client copies of these headers, and the OTA API compares it in constant time, before any lookup, to recognise an [[edge-caller]]. Locally the Vite dev proxy sends it.

A time-limited element added by hand to the `emergency4` or `emergency6` set of the VM's egress firewall table during an outage, with a recorded incident. The allow-list refresh never touches it, a reboot empties it, and `check-vm.sh` reports FAIL while one exists.

`X-Velexis-End-User-IP` and `X-Velexis-End-User-Agent` (at most 512 characters), which a server-side caller adds to every API call so rate limits, lockouts and audit rows name the visitor rather than the server. The portal and platform admin take the IP from the right-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry Caddy wrote (`127.0.0.1` locally) and must send the [[bff-key]] with them (PADR-0019); the OTA admin forwards them through the SDK's `endUser` option, and the OTA API trusts them only from its service caller.

`/etc/velexis/<app>.env`, `root:root 0600`, read only by systemd before it starts a unit as its zone user. It is created once from `deploy/env/<app>.env.example` (`@@…@@` placeholders generated, `CHANGE_ME` values filled by hand), and `velexis-deploy` refuses a release whose templates name a variable the file lacks, or while a value still holds `CHANGE_ME` (`check-vm.sh` reports `FAIL` for it too).

How Velexis stores secrets (Amadeus and Stripe credentials, MFA secrets, payout details, one-time key reveals, traveller documents): each value is encrypted with AES-256-GCM under a fresh 32-byte data key bound to its [[associated-data]], and the data key is wrapped by the current [[kek]] (the master key of `MASTER_KEY_DIR`). The stored `bytea` holds version, KEK id, wrapped data key, IV, tag and ciphertext, `encryption_key_id` repeats the KEK id, and the `secrets:rewrap` CLI command moves data keys to a new master key.

The TEST / LIVE control in the OTA admin's header, stored in the `__Host-vx_env` cookie and sent as `X-Velexis-Environment`. LIVE needs a live OTA and a role other than viewer; a refused live choice falls back to test with a banner.

The list of every API error code with its HTTP status and description (`packages/errors/src/generated/catalogue.ts`), generated from the `x-error-catalogue` of both OpenAPI documents: 74 OTA codes plus 29 platform-only codes, 103 in all. A code with different statuses in the two documents fails generation.

The one JSON body of every API error, `{ error: { code, message, status, requestId, details?, fieldErrors?, supplier? } }`, built by `toErrorEnvelope` (Velexis's own shape, not RFC 7807 `application/problem+json`); anything that is not an [[app-error]] becomes `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` without stack or cause. The SDK maps it to a [[velexis-error]] class by status and code, and a response without it (e.g. a proxy page) gets a code from its status and is never blamed on the supplier.

The focused list at the top of a storefront form (`data-error-summary`) that links to every invalid field; `lib/forms.js` maps the API's `fieldErrors` (JSON pointers) onto controls with `aria-invalid` and messages from `lib/i18n.js` that never repeat the typed value.
The SDK's minified ES2022 module build `dist/velexis-sdk.mjs` (esbuild), with no top-level side effects, imported by npm consumers, the OTA admin and the storefront's production build.

The migration rule that additive (expand) changes ship with the code that needs them and destructive (contract) changes ship in a later release, so the code works with schema versions N-1 and N and a rollback never needs a reverse migration (ADR-0005).

`expectResponseToMatch` from `@velexis/testing`, the OpenAPI response check of every integration test that calls an endpoint: the status must be documented and the body must validate (Ajv 2020, strict) against the operation's response schema. Failures name paths, never values.
`FakeClock` from `@velexis/testing`: a test clock with the backends' `Clock` shape (`now()`), moved with `advance` or `set`, so expiries, deadlines and retries are tested without waiting.
`createFakeFetch`, the SDK's test helper that answers requests from a queue of canned responses and records every request (method, URL, headers, body), so unit tests never touch the network or sleep.

How the OTA worker runs a schedule for every tenant: each scheduler iteration fires one job on the `ota-maintenance` queue that lists the tenants of the schedule's statuses (`active`, `suspended`) in `platform.tenants` and queues one small job per tenant with the deterministic id `<task>:<tenantId>:<bucket>` (the due minute), so a retried or duplicated fan-out adds nothing twice. Not to be confused with [[tenant-fan-out]], the deploy step that migrates every tenant schema.

An airline's named fare bundle for the same flights (e.g. Basic, Classic, Flexible) with different bags, changes, refunds, seats and meals, returned by [[branded-fare-upsell]]. The storefront's offer page shows each as a radio card with the API's total and price difference and keeps the choice in the address as `fare=off_…`.

A configuration flag, `false` by default, that turns a milestone feature on. The platform API's switches are `FEATURE_STRIPE_BILLING`, `FEATURE_OWN_STRIPE`, `FEATURE_SETTLEMENTS`, `FEATURE_OWN_AMADEUS`, `FEATURE_CUSTOM_DOMAINS` and `FEATURE_LIVE_SWITCH`: while one is off its operations answer `403 FEATURE_DISABLED` (with `details.feature`) and its schedules are not registered, and the portal and platform admin hide its areas using `getMe.features` / `adminGetMe.features`. The OTA API has a similar flag, `AIRLINE_CARD_ENABLED`.

A row of `tenant_<key>.fee_rules` that adds an OTA fee to the selling price: `fee_type` `booking_service`, `payment_card`, `ticketing`, `change`, `cancellation` or `ancillary_service`; `calculation` percentage, fixed or both; applied per booking, traveller or segment; `refundable = false` means a cancellation keeps it. Per fee type the first matching active rule applies, and staff manage the rules in the OTA admin's pricing settings.

Per-field problems `{ path (JSON pointer), code, message }` in an [[error-envelope]], allowed only for `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `TRAVELER_DATA_INVALID`, `CONTACT_DATA_INVALID`, `CHECKOUT_INCOMPLETE`, `EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED`, `PASSWORD_TOO_WEAK` and `CURRENT_PASSWORD_INCORRECT` (`FIELD_ERROR_CODES`). The UIs map them onto their form controls.

The Amadeus stub's developer-only `record` command: it captures one response from the Amadeus Enterprise test environment with the developer's own credentials, scrubs personal data, scans the result (`scanForPersonalData`) and writes it as a stub fixture. It refuses to run when `CI` is set or in production.

One itinerary-and-fare option of a [[flight-search]] or an upsell, stored in `tenant_<key>.flight_offers` (id `off_…`, `origin` `search`, `upsell` or `raw`) with the verbatim Amadeus payload, `net_total`, `markup_amount`, `selling_total` and summary columns for filters. Customer scope, and so the storefront, only ever sees the selling amounts.

One Amadeus Flight Offers Search stored in `tenant_<key>.flight_searches` (id `srch_…`) with its criteria, status (`pending`, `completed` or `failed`) and expiry; its offers are then filtered and sorted in SQL without calling Amadeus again. Identical requests within 30 s share one search, and the storefront keeps `search=srch_…` in the address so a reload never searches again.

The owner's one-way switch of an OTA's hosted storefront from test to live (`goLive`, `POST …/go-live` with `{confirm: true}`, owners only, feature `live_switch` / `FEATURE_LIVE_SWITCH`, recent MFA [[step-up]]). In one transaction the platform checks the six [[live-preconditions]] (`422 LIVE_PRECONDITIONS_UNMET` lists the missing ones), sets `tenants.storefront_environment = 'live'`, creates the live payment connection from the test one when there is none and audits `tenant.went_live`; the storefront serves live within 60 seconds and the portal offers no way back.

Finding one booking without an account: `POST /v1/bookings/lookup` (the storefront's `/lookup.html`) with the booking reference or the airline's [[record-locator]] and the last name of any traveller. Every mismatch answers the same `404 NOT_FOUND`; at most five failures per 15 minutes per end-user IP and per reference are allowed (then `429 RATE_LIMITED`), and a match issues a 24-hour [[guest-token]] into `__Host-vx_bt`.

A per-booking access token for travellers without an account: `vxbt_<environment>_` plus 256 random bits, stored only as a SHA-256 in `booking_access_tokens`. It is issued when a guest booking completes (valid 30 days or until 7 days after the last flight, whichever is later) or by a [[guest-lookup]] (24 hours). The hosted storefront keeps up to five `bkg_<id>.<token>` entries, newest first, in the HttpOnly `__Host-vx_bt` cookie; key callers get it in the body and send it as `X-Booking-Token` (SDK `options.bookingToken`).

The portal's answer to `POST /otas/<id>/console/launch` ("Open console"): an auto-submitting HTML form that posts the [[portal-token]] to the OTA admin's `/sso` in the body only. It is served with `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin` and a CSP whose `form-action` allows the OTA admin's origin alone.

A cookie with the `__Host-` prefix (`Secure`, `Path=/`, no `Domain`), which the browser binds to exactly one host, so one OTA's session never reaches another; `SameSite` is set per cookie: `Strict` for the portal's `mfa`, `reset` and `invite` cookies and for every platform admin `__Host-vxa_*` cookie, `Lax` for all the others. Every session token lives in such HttpOnly cookies, out of reach of browser JavaScript: the portal's `__Host-vxp_*` (`at`, `rt`, `mfa`, `reset`, `invite`, `next`, `connect`), the platform admin's `__Host-vxa_*`, the OTA admin's `__Host-vx_staff_at`/`_rt`, `__Host-vx_env` and `__Host-vx_tenant`, and the storefront's `__Host-vx_at`, `__Host-vx_rt` and `__Host-vx_bt`. Only the storefront's double-submit `__Host-vx_csrf` is not HttpOnly.

A server-only API key kind (`hk_…`, `platform.api_keys.kind = 'hosting'`, owned by a portal account rather than one OTA) meant for one deployment serving several OTA domains with `X-Velexis-Host`. The SDK accepts it in server mode, but the MVP OTA API does not serve it and answers `401 INVALID_API_KEY` (hosting keys come after the MVP).

A client-generated header (16–128 characters; the portal and the SDK send a UUID, and the platform also allows only letters, digits, `_` and `-`) that makes a state-changing call safe to retry: the first answer is kept for 24 hours and replayed, and the same key with another body answers `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. The platform API keeps it in Redis (`vx:idem:<accountId>:<key>`, required by `createTenant` and `createCheckoutSession`) and the OTA API in the tenant table `idempotency_keys` (encrypted response, a lease while in flight). The SDK makes one per call and reuses it on every retry; the storefront derives stable keys such as `complete-<chk>-<pay>`.

The optimistic-locking header of an update: it carries the resource `version` the page last read (sent as the ETag `"<n>"`), and the API answers `412 PRECONDITION_FAILED` when the row changed meanwhile, so the UI keeps the input and reloads instead of overwriting. `platform.plans` has no `version` column, so a plan's version is derived from `updated_at` (epoch ms); SDK methods whose operation requires it throw a `TypeError` without `ifMatch`. Amadeus's own simultaneous-update conflict is a different answer, `409 VERSION_CONFLICT`.

The SDK's classic-script build for plain HTML pages (`dist/velexis-sdk.iife.js` plus source map), which only defines the global `window.Velexis` (`Velexis.createVelexisClient(…)`). `ota/sdk/scripts/build.mjs` builds it next to the [[esm-bundle]]; once published it is meant to be loaded from a versioned CDN URL with an SRI hash, or self-hosted.

The one-time display of the `pk_test_…` and `sk_test_…` keys that provisioning's `issue_api_keys` [[post-step]] created and kept envelope-encrypted (`POST …/initial-keys/reveal`, owners only). It works within 24 hours after set-up; the ciphertext is erased at the reveal or by the purge schedule, a second reveal answers `410 KEYS_ALREADY_REVEALED`, and afterwards the keys can only be rolled or revoked.

A pending offer to join an OTA with a [[tenant-role]] (`platform.tenant_invitations`, `ivt_` id, status `pending`, `accepted`, `revoked` or `expired`). It is e-mailed through the [[outbox]] with a 256-bit token of which only the SHA-256 is stored, is valid 7 days, holds a plan seat while pending, and can be accepted only by a signed-in account whose verified e-mail equals the invited address.

The storefront's airline-card page `/checkout/pay-airline.html`, built on its own (one bundle, no shared chunk, no boot, no third-party script, JS ≤ 30 KB gzip) and served with a stricter CSP, `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cache-Control: no-store`. Its card inputs have no `name` and are emptied after every answer and on `pagehide` (OADR-0017), which keeps the storefront side of [[pci-scope]] to this one page.

The common shape of every cross-backend queue message: `v`, `name`, `jobId`, `tenantId`, `requestedAt`, `requestId` and its own `payload`, defined in `@velexis/api-types` with closed JSON Schemas that both backends validate with Ajv. Messages carry ids and small parameters only, never secrets, card data or tokens (ADR-0009 item 10), and an invalid message fails without retry.

The SDK is plain JavaScript whose types live in JSDoc comments (ADR-0019), checked by `tsc --checkJs --strict` with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and emitted as `.d.ts` files. They must match the frozen contract in `docs/velexis-sdk/sdk/src/*.d.ts`, which is never edited.

The key-encryption key that wraps every per-value data key of [[envelope-encryption]] (ADR-0010): a file `master-v<N>.key` (32 random bytes, base64, mode 0400 or 0600) in `MASTER_KEY_DIR`, loaded as KEK id `local:v<N>`. `MASTER_KEY_CURRENT` names the one used for new values while older ones still decrypt; on the VM identical copies live in `/etc/velexis/keys/platform/` and `/etc/velexis/keys/ota/`, and losing it makes every encrypted secret unreadable.

Moving every data key to a new [[kek]] without re-encrypting the data itself: add `master-v<N+1>.key`, make it `MASTER_KEY_CURRENT`, run each backend's `secrets:rewrap` (keyset pages, an optimistic update per row) until `remainingByKekId` is empty, then retire the old key.

A secret kept in its own file instead of an environment variable, checked by `@velexis/config` at start-up: a regular file with no group or other permission bits, valid base64 or PEM, at least `minBytes` long. The config keeps only the path; the content is read where it is used and never appears in an error message.

What a secret API key may call, stored in `platform.api_keys.scopes`: `storefront` (the portal's default; customer operations only, console operations answer `403 SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED`), `console` (console operations together with a staff token) or `console:automation` plus explicit staff permissions such as `bookings:issue` (console operations without a staff token). The OTA API's scope guard enforces it with the `x-scope` and `x-permission` of the [[operations-index]].

An owner's request for live Amadeus access on the shared Velexis account (`requestLiveAmadeus`), which appears as a live `velexis` [[supplier-connection]] in `pending_verification` without an office. The platform admin dashboard lists up to 50, oldest first; assigning a live office from the [[office-pool]] serves it and e-mails the owners.

The six requirements of [[go-live]], each listed in `details.missing` of `422 LIVE_PRECONDITIONS_UNMET` when unmet: `amadeus_live` (an active live Amadeus connection), `payments_live` (an active payment connection that can take live payments), `payout_account` (verified, in Velexis mode only), `plan_live_mode` (`limits.liveMode`), `subscription` (a linked Stripe subscription trialing or active, or an active manual one; a manual trial does not count) and `mfa` (the acting owner's). The portal links each missing one to the page that fixes it.

The storefront's polite ARIA live region (`[data-live-region]` in `partials/states.html`) through which pages announce loading, result counts, price changes, the price-hold warning and payment progress to screen readers.

The Caddyfile snippet `(log_query_filter)` that deletes secret and personal query parameters (`sig`, `token`, `client_secret`, `payment_intent_client_secret`, `setup_intent_client_secret`, `code`, `state`, `q`, `email`, `customerEmail`, `travelerLastName`, `targetId`, `next`) from the URI, the `Referer` and a redirect's `Location` in Caddy's access and error logs.

The SMTP catcher of development, CI and e2e: SMTP on `127.0.0.1:1025`, web UI and API on `http://127.0.0.1:8025`, where every e-mail sent locally lands (verification, invitations, booking confirmations). Tests send to a `uniqueEmail` address and wait for it with `waitForMessage` from `@velexis/testing`; nobody empties the mailbox.

A BullMQ job scheduler of the platform worker, declared in `scheduler.registry.ts` with a cron in UTC (provisioning reconcile, usage flush, purges, domain checks, billing jobs, monthly settlements, office pool level). Schedules of a milestone whose feature switch is off are not registered.

The rule that owners and admins of a live OTA, and platform admins, must keep [[mfa]] on. `MfaEnrolmentGuard` answers `403 MFA_REQUIRED` with `details.reason = enrolment_required` on every `portal`-scope operation (reads included, for their test OTAs too) until they enrol, leaving only the `portal_unverified` operations open; `disableMfa` refuses them with `409 CONFLICT` (`mfa_mandatory`).

A subscription with `billing_provider = 'manual'`, billed outside Stripe: the early-access trial, or a plan a platform admin set with `adminUpdateManualSubscription` (plan, trial end and status Trial, Active or Canceled, with a reason). Only an `active` manual subscription meets go-live's `subscription` precondition (a manual trial does not), and the portal's billing page offers no plan choice for it.

An OTA's rule (`markup_rules`, `mkr_` id) that adds a percentage and/or fixed margin to the Amadeus [[net-price]] of offers matching its scope (routes, carriers, cabins). The pricing engine takes the first matching non-stackable rule by priority as the base and adds every matching stackable rule; the seeded [[default-markup-rule]] (priority 1000, 0 %, empty scope) cannot be deleted or narrowed.

A sensitive identifier shown only in part (for example "IBAN ending in 7947"), exactly as the API returns it (`last4` and similar); the platform admin and the portal never receive the full value outside an audited [[payout-account-reveal]].
Same as [[kek]]. The key-encryption key held outside the database in `MASTER_KEY_DIR` (`MASTER_KEY_CURRENT=local:v1` locally); losing it makes every envelope-encrypted secret unreadable.

The link between an account and an OTA (`platform.tenant_memberships`, `stf_` id) with a [[tenant-role]] (owner, admin, agent, finance or viewer) and a status (`active`, `suspended` or `removed`; removal keeps the row). `TenantRoleGuard` reads it on every tenant request without a cache, and it is what lets an account open that OTA's console through [[sso]]; the OTA admin drops a removed member within 60 seconds.

Two-factor sign-in for Velexis accounts with [[totp]] codes from an authenticator app, set up on the portal's `/account/security` (QR code) with ten single-use [[recovery-code]]s shown once; the TOTP secret is envelope-encrypted in `accounts.mfa_secret_ciphertext`. It is optional for most portal users, mandatory for platform admins, for owners and admins of a live OTA and for opening a live OTA's console, and asked again as a [[step-up]] before sensitive actions.

The short-lived token that the password step of sign-in returns when the account has MFA: kept in Redis as `mfach:<sha256(token)>` for 5 minutes with at most 5 code attempts, and held by the browser in `__Host-vxp_mfa` (portal) or `__Host-vxa_mfa` (platform admin). Only `verifyMfa` with a TOTP or recovery code turns it into a session; an expired one sends the user back to sign-in (`/sign-in?mfa=expired` in the platform admin).

The portal side of [[mandatory-mfa]]: while `getMe.mfaEnrolmentRequired` is true, or a call answers `403 MFA_REQUIRED` with `reason = enrolment_required`, the portal shows only `/mfa-enrolment?next=…` until two-factor authentication is on, then returns to the safe `next` path.

The `schema_migrations` table of each migration set (the `platform` and `reference` schemas and every `tenant_<key>` schema), with one row per applied file: id, description, SHA-256 checksum, phase, status and `execution_ms`. An already-applied file whose checksum changed stops the run with exit code 2; the platform mirrors each tenant's ledger in `platform.tenant_schema_migrations`.

The JSON report of a deploy's tenant fan-out (applied, skipped and failed schemas). `velexis-deploy` publishes it with the OTA CLI command `tenants:report-migrations` as one `tenant.migrated` or `tenant.migration_failed` event per schema on [[platform-tenant-events]] (with `jobId: null`). `tenant.migrated` rows are mirrored into `platform.tenant_schema_migrations` and `platform.tenants.schema_version`; a `tenant.migration_failed` becomes one ops alert e-mail (`OPS_ALERT_EMAIL`) and an audit row `tenant.migration_failed`, and mirrors nothing.

The one migration engine of `@velexis/db`, used locally, in CI, by `velexis-deploy` and by the OTA worker: validated numbered and repeatable (`R__`) files, SHA-256 checksums, one transaction per file, advisory locks and a tenant fan-out with bounded concurrency (ADR-0021). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 checksum mismatch, 3 failure ratio exceeded.
Same as [[money-decimal]]. On the wire money is `{ amount: "123.45", currency: "EUR" }`, a decimal string, never a JavaScript number.

How Velexis handles money: amounts are computed with decimal.js, stored as `numeric(12,2)` columns next to a 3-letter currency, and passed through the APIs and the SDK as decimal strings (`{ amount: "123.45", currency: "EUR" }`), never as JavaScript floats.

One of the 33 SDK methods beyond the frozen TypeScript contract in `docs/velexis-sdk/sdk/src/` (`storefront.listPages`/`getPage`, `checkout.completeWithAirlineCard`, `console.settings.*`, `console.payments.*`, `console.bookings.closeReview`), for 96 + 33 = 129 methods. Each must exist in the working OpenAPI document and is listed in `ota/sdk/docs/extensions.md` (ADR-0019).

The two prices stored side by side on priced offers, checkouts and bookings: net is what Amadeus charges, and selling = net + markup + fees is what the traveller pays. Only console scope may see net amounts and markups; the storefront and customer-scope callers see selling amounts only.

The Amadeus price of an offer before the OTA's markup and fees (the net part of [[net-and-selling-amounts]]). The OTA admin shows it on bookings, PNR imports and shopping, the storefront never does, and airline-card bookings are sold at it (`pricing_mode = 'net'`).

The production VM runs exactly one Node.js major (24, ADR-0029): `provision-vm.sh` installs NodeSource's `node_24.x` line from `NODE_MAJOR` and pins `nodejs` to it at apt priority 1001, and the deploy refuses a release whose recorded Node major differs.

Redis runs with `maxmemory 512mb` and `maxmemory-policy noeviction` (`deploy/redis/velexis.conf`) because BullMQ must never lose keys; so every cache key must carry a TTL, a full Redis refuses writes, and the on-VM health check alerts above 70 % of `maxmemory`.
What a portal OTA page shows to a [[tenant-role]] that may not open it: the role in words, who can change it and the way back to the OTA overview; the navigation also hides the entry for that role.

The subject, HTML and text of one OTA e-mail key, channel and locale (`notification_templates` in the tenant schema), written in a safe Handlebars subset with an allow-list of variables and edited in the OTA admin. A tenant row overrides the code default; a missing locale falls back to the language's row and finally to the English code default, and Reset deletes the row.

The S3-compatible bucket at another provider that holds the VM's `daily/`, `monthly/` and `logs/` objects (encrypted backups and shipped security logs). Its lifecycle rules and object lock enforce retention, and the VM's key may put, list and read but never delete.

The storefront setting `search.maxResults` (stored in `search_defaults`, edited in the OTA admin's storefront settings): 1–250 offers, or empty for the API default of 150 (`DEFAULT_OFFERS_PER_SEARCH`). The storefront's next search asks Amadeus for that many offers.

The OTA API reads or imports Amadeus orders and queues only of the OTA's own offices (owner or queuing office, including Velexis offices it is still releasing); any other office answers `403 OFFICE_NOT_ALLOWED` with nothing of the order. It guards [[pnr-import]], [[raw-amadeus]] reads and queue snapshots.

The Amadeus office ids of Velexis's own Amadeus accounts per environment (`platform.amadeus_offices`), each `available`, `assigned`, `releasing` or `retired`. Provisioning's `assign_amadeus_office` step takes the oldest available test office for each new OTA, ops are warned (dashboard and `amadeus.pool_level` e-mail) when fewer than 3 remain, and locally the platform seed creates `DEV1A0001`–`DEV1A0040`.

A platform admin returning an Amadeus office to `available` (`adminReleaseAmadeusOffice` with `confirmNoOpenBookings: true` and a reason) after checking that no booking with future travel remains on it. Allowed for `releasing` offices and for `assigned` ones whose `velexis` connection is not active (`409 CONFLICT` with `connection_active` otherwise, `not_assigned` for available or retired offices); audited as `amadeus_office.released`.

Caddy obtains a certificate for an unknown storefront host on its first TLS handshake, but only after the platform API's ask endpoint (`GET /internal/tls/ask?domain=`) answers 200. The platform says yes only for tenant sub-domains and verified custom domains of active OTAs, caching yes answers in Redis `tlsask:<host>` for 60 s (refusals in an in-process cache); existing certificates keep working while the platform API is down.

`velexis-healthcheck.timer` runs `healthcheck.sh` every 5 minutes on the VM: unit readiness, failed and waiting jobs, disk, Redis memory (at most 70 % of `maxmemory`), backup age, TLS expiry and, once a day, the live payment pages against the [[payment-page-inventory]]. It mails once through [[velexis-alert]] when a check fails and once when it recovers.

The "Get your OTA ready" list on the portal's OTA overview, computed by `getOnboarding` on every call and never stored (PADR-0018): `email_verified`, `mfa_enabled`, `ota_active`, `api_key`, `storefront_open`, `amadeus_test` and `team_invited`, plus `plan_chosen`, `custom_domain`, `payments_ready` and `live_requested` while their M5 feature switches are on.

`ota/sdk/scripts/operation-overrides.json`: reviewed SDK [[route-table]] values that the OpenAPI document does not carry, each with a reason, such as longer timeouts (60 s, 90 s) and the stricter `retry: "never"` of the airline-card completion.

The `x-scope` extension of every OpenAPI operation, which decides who may call it and so which authentication guard runs: on the platform `public`, `portal_unverified`, `portal`, `platform_admin`, `webhook` or `internal`; in the OTA API `customer`, `console` or `both`. The platform's auth-matrix integration test and the [[operations-index]] check every operation against it.

A generated, frozen list of every operation of both OpenAPI documents (136 OTA and 144 platform operations) with method, path, `x-sdk-method`, `x-scope`, tags, `x-internal`, `x-milestone`, `x-edge-only` and `x-permission`. The route-parity and SDK-parity tests and the OTA scope guard read it, and contract generation rewrites it.

The back office of one OTA (`ota/admin`, Next.js 15 on port 3002, `admin.ota.example.com` in production), opened only through [[sso]] from the portal. Staff work bookings, PNRs, queues, payments, customers and storefront settings through the OTA API's console operations; it is a [[bff]] that keeps the staff tokens in HttpOnly cookies and stores no data of its own.

A BullMQ queue consumed by the OTA worker (`OTA_QUEUES`): `ota-tenant-ops`, `ota-stripe-events`, `ota-payments`, `ota-bookings`, `ota-ticketing`, `ota-notifications`, `ota-documents` and `ota-maintenance`. The platform admin's Queues page shows their counts and failures read-only; a retry answers `403 FORBIDDEN` (`reason: ota_queue`).

The BullMQ queue on which the platform asks the OTA worker to `tenant.provision`, `tenant.migrate`, `tenant.suspend` or `tenant.resume` a tenant schema. Each dispatch attempt of a [[provisioning-job]] is one BullMQ job `<jobId>-<attempt>` carrying a [[job-envelope]] of ids; the answer comes back on [[platform-tenant-events]].

The VM's nftables table `inet velexis_egress` (output policy drop) that lets the services reach only the hosts of `deploy/egress/allowed-hosts.conf` and logs every other attempt as `VELEXIS-EGRESS-DENY`; `velexis-egress-refresh.timer` re-resolves the host addresses every 2 minutes.

The transactional e-mail outbox: an e-mail is a row written in the same transaction as the business change (`platform.email_outbox` on the platform, `notifications` in each tenant schema) and sent later by the worker with retries, so an SMTP outage never fails the change and nothing is lost. Links with tokens are envelope-encrypted and erased once the row is sent or failed; the platform worker sends on `platform-emails`, and the OTA worker claims rows with a 5-minute lease.

`tools/reference-data/data/overrides.csv`, the only hand-edited reference-data file: lines `table,key,column,value` that fix single values between snapshot refreshes. Overrides are validated like the data and win in the row the [[reference-loader]] writes.

The generic attack rules the [[coraza-waf]] loads in Caddy: OWASP CRS v4 at paranoia level 1 with the default inbound anomaly threshold 5 (one critical match blocks), the `REQUEST-*` rules plus `RESPONSE-980-CORRELATION`. Its log data is replaced by `logdata.conf`, so no matched value is ever logged.

The named UI state a storefront page shows for an API error (`suspended`, `unknown-host`, `unavailable`, `rate-limited`, `price-changed`, `sold-out`, …), chosen from the error code by `pageStateFor(error)`. `suspended` and `unknown-host` replace the whole page; the others sit inline, with Retry where retrying can help.

The SDK contract test `ota/sdk/test/contract/parity.test.js`: the set of `x-sdk-method` names in the working OpenAPI document (without `x-internal` and `x-sdk-exclude` operations) must equal the methods of a client instance, all 129. Strict since SDK-013: an operation that gains an `x-sdk-method` gets its SDK method in the same change.

An OTA's Stripe set-up per environment (`platform.payment_provider_connections`, `ppc_` id): [[account-mode]] (`velexis`, `connect_standard` or `api_keys`), account reference, encrypted keys, capabilities, [[statement-descriptor-suffix]] and status (`pending`, `active`, `disabled` or `error`; only `active` can charge). Provisioning creates the `velexis` test connection, and [[go-live]] copies it to live when no live one exists.

Stripe's embedded card form, mounted only on the storefront's `/checkout/pay-card.html` with the payment's publishable key and client secret. Card data stays inside Stripe's iframes (the page has no card input of its own), and [[3-d-secure]] runs during `confirmPayment`.

The OTA API's interface (`createSession`, `refresh`, `capture`, `void`, `refund`) that hides Stripe in its three [[account-mode]]s behind one shape, plus the inert airline-card gateway, where the airline charges the card.

Stripe's payment object, created by `checkout.createPayment` with manual capture and Velexis metadata, confirmed by Stripe.js in the browser and re-read by `checkout.complete`. The card is only authorised until the Amadeus order exists, then captured, or voided when the booking fails.

The storefront build output `dist/payment-page-inventory.json` listing every page's scripts, hashes and headers (PCI DSS 6.4.3): the build fails on an unreviewed page or third-party script, the release ships it as `storefront/payment-page-inventory.json`, and the daily health check compares the live `pay-card.html` and `pay-airline.html` with it (PCI DSS 11.6.1).

The OTA's bank account for Velexis-mode settlements (`platform.tenant_payout_accounts`): IBAN or local account and routing numbers, envelope-encrypted, with only `last4` in clear. Owners set it with a step-up and every real change returns it to `pending_review`; a platform admin verifies or rejects it, and a verified one is needed for go-live in Velexis mode and to approve a positive settlement statement.

Showing an OTA's full IBAN/BIC or account and routing numbers to a platform admin (`adminRevealPayoutAccount`) who gave a 5–500 character reason and a recent MFA step-up. The console keeps the values in memory for 60 seconds with no copy button, and every reveal is audited as `payout_account.revealed`.

The folder `ota/docs/pci/`: scope, calendar of scans, tests and reviews, data flow, script inventory, incident response and responsibility matrix for the airline-card path, the evidence from which Velexis fills in its SAQ D for Service Providers. Its line references into the code are kept current with the [[pci-refs-checker]].

`tools/ci/check-pci-refs.mjs` checks that every line reference of the [[pci-evidence-pack]] still points at the lines that hold its quoted code, and `fix-pci-refs.mjs` moves the references to where the quotes now are. They are run by hand at reviews and integrations, not in CI.

The parts of Velexis that see full card data: only the airline-card path (the [[isolated-payment-page]], the OTA API's completion route and the in-memory transit to Amadeus) and the VM controls around it (ADR-0027). That path never stores, logs or queues the card; Stripe card payments stay inside Stripe's iframes.

The storefront confirmation page mode "We are confirming your booking with the airline" (address parameter `pending=1`), shown after a [[supplier-timeout]] or while a completion is in progress. It polls the booking every 10 s for up to 30 minutes and drops `pending=1` once the booking is decided.

The size limits `check-budgets.mjs` enforces after every storefront build, gzip-compressed per page: JS ≤ 60 KB (30 KB on `checkout/pay-airline.html`), CSS ≤ 20 KB, HTML ≤ 20 KB, and at most 2 font families and 120 KB of woff2. The Lighthouse targets (run by hand) are LCP ≤ 2.5 s, CLS ≤ 0.1 and INP ≤ 200 ms.

A Velexis price plan (`platform.plans`): code, monthly and annual prices, trial days, `limits` (`staffSeats`, `apiKeys`, `customDomains`, `liveMode`) and `features` JSON, `settlement_fee_bps` and Stripe price ids. Limits gate portal actions and go-live; public active plans appear on the portal's pricing page, retired plans keep their OTAs, and `early_access` (free, test mode only) is the only plan before M5.

The linter and progress report of the agent task plans (`tools/plan-lint/plan-lint.mjs`, `pnpm plan:lint`): it checks task blocks, their fields, dependencies and the done marker ` ✅`, and `--remaining` lists the ready tasks of the lowest open milestone (ADR-0025).

A normal Velexis account with `accounts.is_platform_admin = true`, an active status and MFA on; only such accounts pass the platform admin console's password step and may call `/v1/admin/**`, where every call is audited. The flag is granted by `adminGrantAdmin` or the `admin:grant` CLI command and re-read on every request, so revoking it acts at the next call.

The Velexis staff console (`platform/admin`, Next.js 15 on `127.0.0.1:3001`, `admin.platform.example.com` in production) where platform admins run OTAs, provisioning jobs, plans and billing, the Amadeus office pool, settlements, domains, accounts, queues and the audit log. It is a [[bff]] over the platform API's `/v1/admin` surface and stores nothing itself.

The Kysely instance of `@velexis/db` for the `platform.*` and `reference.*` tables, always queried by schema-qualified name. Tenant tables are not in its types, so it cannot reach them; tenant data goes through [[tenant-tx]] instead.

A stable code of the platform API's [[error-envelope]] (`CONFLICT`, `REAUTH_REQUIRED`, `FEATURE_DISABLED`, `MFA_REQUIRED`, …), often refined by `details.reason`; the list is generated in `@velexis/errors`. The portal and the platform admin never show the API's message text: their `lib/strings.ts` maps every code to their own sentence, and a test fails when a code has none.

A BullMQ queue consumed by the platform worker (`PLATFORM_QUEUES`): `platform-tenant-events`, `platform-emails`, `platform-stripe-events`, `platform-domains`, `platform-connections`, `platform-settlements` and `platform-maintenance`. The platform admin shows each at `/queues/<queue>` and may retry its failed jobs.

The `platform` PostgreSQL schema owned by the platform backend: accounts, tenants, memberships, invitations, API keys, domains, supplier and payment connections, Amadeus accounts and offices, plans, subscriptions, settlements, provisioning jobs, the e-mail outbox and the audit log. The OTA backend only reads the tables `R__ota_read_access.sql` grants it and never writes them.

The by-hand performance smoke test of the platform API on a scratch stack (`tools/perf/platform-smoke.mjs`): six open-loop phases with p95 targets, the RSS of each unit against its `MemoryMax`, and the share of time spent in garbage collection, measured by a preloaded `gc-observer.cjs`.

The BullMQ queue on which the OTA worker answers the platform: `tenant.provisioned`, `tenant.provision_failed`, `tenant.migrated`, `tenant.migration_failed`, `tenant.suspended` and `tenant.resumed`. The platform worker consumes it with concurrency 4, settles the [[provisioning-job]] and runs the [[post-step]]s; a deploy's [[migration-report]] is published onto it with `jobId: null`.

The second process of the platform backend (`dist/worker.js`, systemd unit `velexis-platform-worker`, health on `127.0.0.1:3101`): it consumes the seven [[platform-queue]]s (tenant events, e-mails, Stripe events, domain checks, connection verification, settlements, maintenance), runs the schedules and serves no API. Many portal and admin actions only finish once it runs.

A group of e2e journeys with its own base URL in `tools/e2e/playwright.config.ts`: `portal`, `platform-admin`, `storefront`, `ota-admin`, and the Stripe-network projects `portal-stripe` and `storefront-stripe`. A project whose part of the stack is not started is not defined.

Staff look up an Amadeus order made outside Velexis by [[record-locator]] in the OTA admin and import it as a booking (`channel = import`, ticketing `manual_review`, no payment, priced by markup rules, at net or at an override), audited as `booking.import`. Orders of offices that are not the OTA's are refused by [[office-isolation]].

The Velexis customer website (`platform/frontend`, Next.js 15 on port 3000, `platform.example.com` in production) where people sign up, create and pay for an OTA, manage API keys, domains, connections, team and billing, go live and open the OTA admin. It is a [[bff]] of the platform API that keeps tokens in HttpOnly `__Host-vxp_*` cookies and stores no data of its own.

The portal's own words for each platform API error code (`ERROR_MESSAGES` in `platform/frontend/src/lib/strings.ts`); the API's message text is dropped in `lib/api.ts`, so pages never show a raw API error.

The single-use token that carries a member from the portal into the OTA admin: `createConsoleToken` makes `ptk_` plus 43 base62 characters (256 bits) and stores `ptk:<sha256>` in Redis for 60 s. The [[hand-off-page]] posts it to the OTA admin's `/sso`, and the OTA API redeems it once with `GETDEL` in `console.auth.signIn` (`grantType: "portal_token"`) for a staff session.

One of the six idempotent platform steps that run after `tenant.provisioned`, in order: `record_migrations`, `assign_amadeus_office`, `create_payment_connection`, `issue_api_keys`, `activate` and `notify`. Each runs in its own short transaction under the job's row lock and is logged in `provisioning_jobs.steps`, so a crash or a second delivery resumes at the first step not done.

Every application id is a 2–4 letter type prefix plus a CSPRNG ULID: `ten_`, `acc_`, `stf_`, `ivt_`, `key_`, `job_` on the platform; `srch_`, `off_`, `prc_`, `chk_`, `pay_`, `bkg_`, `cus_` in the tenant schemas, each checked by a `CHECK` constraint. Some OTA ids (searches, offers, priced offers, checkouts, payments) also serve as capability ids for guests.

The storefront price page's countdown (`role="timer"`) to the [[priced-offer]]'s `expiresAt`, shown as "Price held for mm:ss" and announced once when five minutes are left. At zero "Price expired" disables Continue and offers Re-price.

A difference between a plan and its linked Stripe price (amount, currency, interval, archived or missing), found when prices are linked or checked and stored with the plan. The platform admin shows each warning in words next to the price; it never blocks a save and does not change the plan's version.

The confirmed price of chosen offers from Amadeus Flight Offers Price (`priced_offers`, `prc_` id): totals, taxes, fees, `price_changed`, [[booking-requirements]], bags, card fees and fare rules, with selling = net + markup + fees. It expires at `min(now + offer_ttl_minutes, end of the earliest lastTicketingDate)` (`410 OFFER_EXPIRED` after that); the price page and the [[checkout]] start from it, and extras create a child priced offer.

How a checkout or booking was priced (`pricing_mode`): `markup_rules` (normal selling prices), `net` (the Amadeus total with no markup or OTA fees, used for the airline card, where the airline charges the card) or `override` (a price staff set at a console import or creation). On the storefront, switching the payment method switches the mode.

The host on which an OTA's storefront sessions are created when it has a verified primary [[custom-domain]]: because cookies are host-only, sign-in and sign-up opened on the OTA's sub-domain `location.replace` to the same path on the primary host before any session starts, and e-mail links use the primary host too.

The GitHub Actions environment `production` that holds `DEPLOY_HOST`, `DEPLOY_USER`, `DEPLOY_SSH_KEY` and `DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS`, requires the developer's approval and allows only `main` and `v*` tags; the deploy workflow's deploy job runs in it.

`deploy/scripts/provision-vm.sh`: idempotent provisioning of a blank Ubuntu 24.04 VM in named steps (packages, node, harden, users, postgres, redis, caddy, keys, database, envfiles, scripts, caddyconf, summary; `ssh` and `egress` only when named). It never overwrites a key, env file or generated secret, and pins Node, Redis and Caddy through apt.

Creating an OTA's backend state: the platform records a [[provisioning-job]] and enqueues `tenant.provision` on [[ota-tenant-ops]], the OTA worker creates and migrates the `tenant_<key>` schema and answers `tenant.provisioned`, and the platform worker runs the [[post-step]]s (office, payment connection, test keys, activate, notify). The portal's set-up page follows it step by step.

A row of `platform.provisioning_jobs` (`job_` id) for one lifecycle operation of an OTA: kind `provision`, `migrate`, `suspend` or `resume`; status `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed` or `canceled`; attempts, a 15-minute lease and a step log. Each dispatch attempt goes to the OTA worker as BullMQ job `<jobId>-<attempt>` on [[ota-tenant-ops]]; the platform admin shows the step log and offers Retry on failed and Cancel on queued jobs.
