A browser-safe API key (`pk_test_…`/`pk_live_…`, `platform.api_keys.kind = 'publishable'`) limited to customer-scope operations and to the origins in its `allowed_origins`; a browser request from another origin answers `403 ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, and the OTA API answers CORS for the listed origins only.

A named BullMQ queue in Redis (keys `vx:<queue>:…`), owned by the backend whose worker consumes it and named `<owner>-<topic>` (ADR-0009): the seven [[platform-queue]]s and the eight [[ota-queue]]s, including the cross-backend pair [[ota-tenant-ops]] and [[platform-tenant-events]]. The platform admin's Queues page shows them all.

The OTA worker's job that every 15 minutes, per active tenant, reads the monitored Amadeus office queues (5 queues per job, continued in further jobs) and stores a [[queue-snapshot]] of each; a queue that fails is counted and read again at the next run.

One stored read of an Amadeus office queue (Queue List) in `queue_snapshots` (`qsn_` id), taken by staff ("Read now from Amadeus") or by the 15-minute [[queue-poller]]. Each PNR in it links to the OTA's booking or offers an import, and snapshots are kept 30 days.

Redis counters that limit calls: Amadeus token buckets per credential set (`rl:amadeus:cred:<credId>:<env>`, 20/s, burst 20) and per tenant (`rl:amadeus:ten:<tenantId>:<env>`, 5/s, burst 10), where background calls must leave half of each burst for the calls a person waits for, plus the API throttlers `rl:ota_<limit>:<digest>`. When Redis is down the limited calls answer `503` instead of skipping the limit.

Console read operations under `/v1/console/amadeus` that pass a request through to Amadeus as is (flight search, availability, upsell, price, order GET, by reference, Queue List) and return net prices, subject to [[office-isolation]]; raw writes are deferred after the MVP.

A platform admin operation that requires a free-text reason (`AdminReason`): 5–500 characters after trimming, kept in the `details` of its audit row. Examples: suspend or resume an OTA, disable an account, remove a domain, release an office, reveal bank details, adjust a settlement.
The platform admin's dialog that collects the mandatory reason of a [[reason-action]] (and extra fields such as the suspension kind) and refuses anything outside 5–500 code points before any call.

The result of a booking [[reconciliation]] in `bookings.reconcile_outcome`: `found` (the order was recorded), `not_found` (the payment voided and the booking failed) or `manual_review` (staff decide; typically an airline-card booking). Staff close a manual review in the OTA admin as "Order found" or "Not booked".

The platform's `provisioning.reconcile` schedule (every 5 minutes), the safety net of provisioning: it re-checks `running` [[provisioning-job]]s whose 15-minute lease ended (extending the lease while the BullMQ attempt is still under way, otherwise failing or re-queuing it) and dispatches due `queued` jobs. Not to be confused with booking [[reconciliation]] in the OTA backend.

The OTA worker's search for an Amadeus order whose create answer was lost (a [[supplier-timeout]]): the booking stays `pending` with `reconcile_until`, and the worker reads the OTA's booking queue (Queue List) and orders by reference, matching the remark `VELEXIS <reference>`, instead of ever retrying order creation blindly. A found order is recorded, a not-found Stripe booking fails and its authorisation is voided, and the rest go to [[reconciliation-review]].

The state of a booking whose order-create answer was lost and that [[reconciliation]] could not settle: `pending` with `reconcile_outcome = manual_review`. Staff close it in the OTA admin (`console.bookings.closeReview`) with "Order found" (giving the record locator) or "Not booked" (with a note).

The airline/Amadeus reservation code of an order (PNR): 5–8 upper-case letters or digits such as `L2P9XC`, stored in `bookings.record_locator` (unique per environment and origin system). Staff use it for PNR lookup, import and review closure, and guests may give it instead of the booking reference in a [[guest-lookup]].

One of ten single-use [[mfa]] codes (80-bit random, stored SHA-256 hashed in `platform.account_recovery_codes`) shown once when MFA is turned on. It replaces a TOTP code at the sign-in code step ("Use a recovery code instead") when the authenticator is lost, never for a step-up, and regenerating replaces all ten.

The single list of pino paths in `@velexis/logger` censored as `[REDACTED]` in every log line of every service: passwords, tokens, secrets, card objects to depth 8, credential headers, bank and MFA fields. A new sensitive field means a new path plus a test.

The deep-copy redactor of `@velexis/logger` applied before a payload copy is stored (supplier requests, order snapshots, staff actions, idempotency records, payment events, notifications): card numbers cut to the last 4, CVC, holder and expiry dropped, tokens and secrets `[REDACTED]`. It masks by key name and never looks into free text: a console note, reason or remark that holds a card number is refused instead (`card_data`, `holdsCardNumber`).

The committed CSV files of the `reference` schema (currencies, countries, time zones, cities, airports, airlines, aircraft) under `tools/reference-data/data/`, built by hand from OpenTravelData (CC BY 4.0) and Unicode CLDR with their checksums in `SOURCES.md` (ADR-0024). CI, deploys and tests never download it; [[overrides-csv]] patches single values.

The CLI of `tools/reference-data` that loads the snapshot into `reference.*` in one transaction as `velexis_platform_app`, table by table in foreign-key order: release moved unique codes, upsert changed rows, deactivate (`is_active = false`) missing codes, never delete. A second run reports zero changes.

The shared, read-only PostgreSQL schema `reference` with travel reference data: `reference.airports`, `airlines`, `cities`, `countries`, `currencies` (with their minor-unit exponent), `time_zones` and `aircraft` (`platform/backend/migrations/reference/0001_baseline.sql`). The [[reference-loader]] fills it (`pnpm db:seed:reference`, the `@velexis/reference-data` package in `tools/reference-data`), and every tenant transaction sees it next to its own schema through `search_path = '<schema>, reference'`.

All the refresh tokens descended from one sign-in: every refresh rotates the token into a new generation, and presenting an already rotated one revokes the whole family (`401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED`, see [[refresh-token-reuse]]). Families live in `platform.account_sessions` (`family_id`, the access token's `sid`; at most 30 days in the portal, 12 hours in the platform admin), in `tenant_<key>.customer_sessions` for storefront customers (12 hours, 30 days with remember-me) and in Redis `staffsess:<familyId>` for OTA admin staff (12 hours).

Reuse detection on refresh: a refresh token that was already rotated, presented again, revokes its whole [[refresh-family]] in a committed transaction before the answer `401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED`, so the family's newest token stops working too (`customer_sessions.revoke_reason = 'rotation_reuse'` on the OTA side; for staff the Lua script deletes `staffsess:<familyId>` and writes `staffdeny:<familyId>`). A stolen rotated token therefore ends the session instead of reaching it; the portal's and the OTA admin's [[single-flight-refresh]] and the SDK's [[client-family]] rules exist so that legitimate clients never trip it.

The self-contained build of one commit, `release/<sha>/`, assembled in CI by `deploy/scripts/pack-release.sh` after `pnpm build`: `RELEASE.json`, [[sha256sums]], `deploy/`, `db/` (the migration CLI), `migrations/{platform,reference,tenant}/`, `reference-data/`, both backends, the three Next.js standalone apps, the static storefront and `caddy/bin/caddy`. [[velexis-deploy]] verifies the upload in `/srv/velexis/incoming/<sha>`, activates it as `/srv/velexis/releases/<sha>/` behind the `/srv/velexis/current` link and keeps the last five releases.

An `R__<name>.sql` file of the platform or reference migration set (ADR-0021) that may contain only GRANT, REVOKE and COMMENT ON statements: the runner applies it after the numbered files whenever its SHA-256 differs from its `platform.schema_migrations` row (phase `repeatable`), and unlike a numbered file it may be edited. The one in use, `R__ota_read_access.sql`, grants `velexis_ota_app` SELECT on the platform tables and the safe `accounts` columns the OTA backend reads; tenant sets have no repeatable files.

The first step of CI's `build-test` job, run before `pnpm install` so a broken rule fails in seconds: no session-level `SET search_path` (or `set_config('search_path', …, false)`) outside `packages/db/`, every `0001_baseline.sql` byte-identical to its reference file in `docs/velexis-sdk/db/`, and no pull-request change under `docs/velexis-sdk/` or `docs/amadeus-api/`. Focused tests (`it.only` and friends) are caught by an ESLint rule in `pnpm lint` and by Vitest under `CI` instead.

The heart of an SDK client (`ota/sdk/src/internal/client.js`): it validates the client options, picks the session mode (cookie, token or server) once, and `core.call(op, params, options)` turns a method's params into a request by its [[route-table]] entry (path params URI-encoded, query params, `ifMatch` → `If-Match`, the rest as a JSON or multipart body). A list operation (one with a `cursor` query param) resolves with a `Page`; `internal/http.js` then sends the request with retries.

`client.request(method, path, { query, body, options })`: the SDK's low-level call of any API path (starting with `/`, never `//` or a backslash) with the client's credentials, headers, retries and error mapping. GET, PUT and DELETE are retried; POST and PATCH only when the caller passes its own `idempotencyKey`, because the SDK cannot know whether the endpoint honours a generated one, and `environment` is added on `/v1/console/…` paths.

The id that ties one API request's log lines, error and rows together: `pinoHttpOptions` of `@velexis/logger` keeps a valid incoming `X-Request-Id` (`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{8,128}$`) or generates a UUID, returns it as `X-Request-Id` on every answer and puts it in every log line and every [[error-envelope]] (`requestId`). The OTA API also stores it on staff actions, supplier requests and events, the OTA admin shows it with every error message, and the SDK exposes it as `error.requestId` and to `onResponse`.

The optional last argument of every SDK method (`RequestOptions` in `ota/sdk/src/shared.js`): `signal`, `idempotencyKey` (16 to 128 characters, generated when omitted), `timeoutMs`, `headers`, `accessToken`, `bookingToken`, `locale`, `currency`, the Next.js `next` and `cache` fetch options, `endUser` and `host`. They are validated like the client options, so an unknown or invalid entry throws a `TypeError` before any request is sent.

The SDK client option `onResponse`, called after every HTTP response, retries included, with `{ method, path, status, requestId, durationMs }` and never headers or bodies; its failures, a rejected promise included, are ignored so a metrics bug never fails a call. It is the integrator's hook for logs and metrics (the OTA admin uses it in `lib/velexis.ts`), since the SDK itself never logs.

The rehearsed rebuild from last night's off-VM [[backup-set]] on a scratch VM that can reach neither Amadeus nor Stripe, with a measured recovery time of 4 hours or less (RTO) and the restore of one tenant. `velexis-restore drill <dir> --identity <key>` (`deploy/scripts/restore.sh`) restores into a scratch database, runs its checks and appends the figures and duration to a drill log; ADR-0007 asks for it in M6 and then every quarter (PCI DSS 12.10.1).

The platform admin's re-fetch of one Stripe-billed [[subscription]] from Stripe without waiting for a webhook (`adminResyncSubscription`, audited as `subscription.resynced`), offered only on a subscription that has a Stripe subscription. A manual subscription answers `409 CONFLICT` (`details.reason = manual`), a row billing sync cannot apply `409`, and a Stripe failure `502 PROVIDER_ERROR` with nothing changed.

The response header (seconds or an HTTP date) that says when to try again, sent with `429 RATE_LIMITED` and, on the platform, with the sign-in lockout's `423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED`. The SDK waits that long instead of its own back-off before a retry, ends the call at once when it asks for more than 30 seconds, and exposes it as `RateLimitError.retryAfterSeconds`.

The SDK's automatic retries (`ota/sdk/src/internal/http.js`): only requests of retry class `safe` (GET) or `idempotent` (PUT, DELETE, a call with an `Idempotency-Key`, or a POST the document marks `x-idempotent-by-design`) are retried, at most `maxRetries` times (default 2), on 429, 503, 504 and network errors, waiting 0.5 s × 2^(n−1) capped at 8 s ± 20 % or the [[retry-after]]. Timeouts, aborts, a POST or PATCH without a key and `checkout.completeWithAirlineCard` are never retried, and every retry of a call sends the same idempotency key.

Same as [[safe-next-path]]. The `next` query parameter that brings a person back to the page they asked for after sign-in (portal, platform admin, the OTA admin's `/auth/refresh`, storefront); only a same-origin relative path survives the check, anything else falls back to the app's default page.

The 10 seconds (`ROTATION_WINDOW_MS` in `ota/sdk/src/internal/session.js`) after the API rotated a refresh token for a client of an SDK [[client-family]], during which any client of that family about to present the old token takes the family's newest tokens instead (a late request of the same visitor that still carries the old cookie). After it, only a client that held the old token as its own string follows the rotation; any other sends it, and the API's [[refresh-token-reuse]] detection revokes the session.

The contract test that fails when a backend's NestJS routes and its OpenAPI document disagree: a route without `@OpenApiOperation`, a wrong method or path, or an operation that no route binds. It keeps the contract-first rule honest for every milestone (PADR-0016).

The generated `ota/sdk/src/internal/operations.js`: one frozen entry per [[x-sdk-method]] (129 today) with method, path, path/query/header params, idempotency, retry class, timeout, the console `environment` flag and body kind. `scripts/generate-operations.mjs` regenerates it from the OTA OpenAPI document; it is never edited by hand, and CI fails when it is out of date.

The storefront's configuration from `storefront.get` (`GET /v1/storefront`): branding, locales, currencies, features, legal links, support, payment methods and the `environment`. Each page reads it once and keeps it 5 minutes in sessionStorage `vx.storefront.config` (errors are never cached, and any `403 TENANT_SUSPENDED` drops it); the API caches its answer in Redis `t:<tenantId>:<env>:sf:<locale>` for 5 minutes.

The open-redirect guard on every `next` return path: `safeNextPath` (portal and platform admin `lib/session.ts`, OTA admin `lib/session.ts`) and the storefront's `safeNext` (`src/lib/url.js`) keep a value only when it is a same-origin relative path (one leading `/`, no `//`, backslash or control character, at most 2048 characters) that is still one after URL normalisation, so `/.//evil.example` or `https://…` is dropped. A dropped value falls back to the app's default page (`/dashboard` in the portal, `/` on the storefront).

A preset filter of the OTA admin's `/bookings` list, defined in `bookings/views.ts` as URL parameters: the Needs attention group (Ticketing problems, Reconciliation review, Deadline within 24 h, Cancellation requested, Schedule changed) and Lists (All bookings, To issue and the other presets). Because the URL is the state, every view is a link staff can share, and the dashboard's counts use the same filters.

`ota/sdk/release/sdk-publish.draft.yml`, the draft GitHub Actions workflow that will publish `@velexis/ota-sdk`: tests, build, one packed tarball, then `npm publish --provenance --access public` (a dry run by default). It never runs where it is: the owner approves it line by line and it then moves unchanged to `.github/workflows/sdk-publish.yml`; `tools/ci/sdk-draft-pins.test.mjs` keeps its action pins in step with the live workflows, and `ota/sdk/release/CHANGES.md` records each revision and its SHA-256.

The SDK's Vitest smoke tests (`ota/sdk/test/smoke/`, `pnpm --filter @velexis/ota-sdk test:smoke`) that call a running OTA API backed by the Amadeus stub, in token mode and in server mode, with the keys the OTA backend's [[dev-seed]] prints. They run nightly in the e2e workflow (`.github/workflows/e2e.yml`) and on demand, never on pull requests.

A safety check inside `tenantTx` of `@velexis/db`: in every environment except production (`APP_ENV`), the first statement of a tenant transaction compares the pooled connection's `search_path` with the role's default and throws `SearchPathLeakError` before the callback runs when a session-level `SET search_path` leaked into the pool. With the [[repository-guards]] rule in CI it keeps one OTA's schema from leaking into another request.

A server-only OTA API key, `sk_test_…` or `sk_live_…` (an [[api-key]] sent as `X-Api-Key`), never used in a browser. Alone it runs in customer scope; with a staff token it reaches console operations in console scope, a key with the `console:automation` scope calls console operations itself within its listed permissions, and a key scoped `storefront` gets `403 SCOPE_NOT_ALLOWED` on every console operation. The SDK refuses a `secretKey` where `document` exists and uses it in [[server-mode]].

`velexis-logreview` (`deploy/scripts/log-review.sh`), run every hour at :20 by `velexis-log-review.timer`: it reads the shipped security entries with its own journald cursor and mails immediate alerts through [[velexis-alert]] (root login, a new SSH key, a change under `/etc/velexis/keys`, an AIDE change outside a deploy, `aide-error`, `aide-stale`, failed shipments, bursts of egress refusals and more). At its first run after 06:00 UTC each day it also sends a summary of the last 24 hours (PCI DSS 10.4.1).

`velexis-shiplogs` (`deploy/scripts/ship-logs.sh`), run every hour at :05: it turns the journal's security entries since its saved cursor (sshd, sudo, logins, auditd, Caddy access and WAF lines, egress refusals, fail2ban, AIDE, failed units, backend security events) into JSON lines, blanks every query value of WAF lines, compresses them with zstd, encrypts them with age and uploads the chunk to `<remote>/logs/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/` (`rclone copy --immutable`). Daily copies stay 90 days on the VM in `/var/log/velexis/security/`; the bucket keeps 12 months.

The OTA API's in-memory wrapper of an airline card for the one request that uses it (`SensitiveCard`): `toJSON()`, `toString()`, `Symbol.toPrimitive` and `util.inspect` all answer `[redacted card]`, so no log line, JSON body, cache or queue can carry the number. It is passed to Flight Create Orders and blanked in a `finally` block, after which every read refuses it.

A Next.js `"use server"` function that a form posts to (`actions.ts` files, read with `useActionState`); in the portal, the platform admin and the OTA admin every mutation is one. It checks the fields with Zod (the OTA admin first calls `requireStaff(permission)`), calls one API operation server side with the session's token, and answers a state (field errors mapped from the API's JSON pointers, a `stepUp` request, a success) or redirects, instead of throwing the API error.

The SDK session mode for server code, chosen when the client gets a secret key (the OTA admin's [[service-key]] included) or a hosting key; `secretKey` is refused where `globalThis.document` exists. Tokens come per client or per call through `withOptions` and [[request-options]], `endUser` forwards the visitor's IP and user agent, and the OTA admin uses it with `sessionKind: "staff"` and `environment`.

`OTA_ADMIN_SERVICE_KEY`, the OTA admin server's own `sk_…` credential, sent as `X-Api-Key` through the SDK's `secretKey`. The OTA API treats it as the service caller only on a direct loopback connection without `X-Forwarded-For` or `X-Forwarded-Host`, only on console operations, and only with a staff token of the tenant (except `console.auth.signIn`), the required [[x-velexis-environment]] and the end user's forwarded IP and user agent.

SDK client options awaited around refreshes: `onSessionRefreshed` gets the new token pair after the SDK refreshed (so the integrator can store it), `onSessionExpired` is called once when a refresh is refused with 401, and `onStaffSessionRefreshed` gets the whole `ConsoleStaffSession` after an automatic staff refresh. Only the client whose call started the refresh reports it, and an error a hook throws is ignored.

What `auth.signIn`, `auth.refresh` and `auth.changePassword` resolve with (`AuthSessionResult`). In token and server mode the SDK adopts its tokens as the client's session and reports them to `onSessionRefreshed` (the family's newest pair when another client has rotated them meanwhile); in cookie mode the API sets the cookies and the result comes back without token fields.

Velexis's monthly statement of what it owes an OTA for card payments it collected in Velexis [[account-mode]] (`platform.settlements`, `stl_…`, with `settlement_lines`, per currency and environment): captured payments minus refunds, disputes, Stripe and Velexis fees, plus adjustments and amounts carried forward. Drafts are built from Stripe balance transactions; platform admins approve them, pay by bank transfer outside the system to the verified [[payout-account]] and mark them paid (statuses `draft`, `approved`, `paid`, `carried_forward`, `void`), and owners and finance members see them with a CSV in the portal.

A manual signed line (`type = 'adjustment'`) a platform admin adds to a draft [[settlement]] (`adminAddSettlementAdjustment`) with a description the OTA sees and a reason. The amount is a non-zero decimal string that fits `numeric(12,2)` and has no more decimals than the currency's minor units in `reference.currencies` (0 for JPY, else `422`); regenerating the month's drafts rebuilds them from scratch and drops adjustments.

The portal page `/otas/<id>/setup` that follows a new OTA's [[provisioning-job]] every 2 seconds (`ProvisioningProgress`, `SETUP_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`), offers owners Retry after a failure and, with Stripe billing, the Stripe Checkout hand-off for the plan. Once provisioning succeeds it shows the one-time reveal of the OTA's test API keys.

The checksum file of a [[release-folder]], listing the SHA-256 of every regular file `pack-release.sh` packed, so nothing may be added to the folder afterwards. [[velexis-deploy]] checks the upload against it before changing anything and refuses a changed, missing, unlisted or special file.

The OTA admin's `/shopping` page for staff on the phone with a customer: raw, read-only Amadeus flight offers, availability, branded fares and price confirmation at net prices, each raw read audited by the API. Nothing is stored or booked; booking on behalf of a customer is deferred.

A secret the portal shows exactly once, taken from the answer of the action that created it (a new API key, MFA recovery codes, the MFA set-up key, the OTA's initial test keys): `SecretRevealPanel` holds it in React state with a copy button and a warning, it is never stored, cached or logged, and a reload never shows it again.

The test helper `signedStripeEvent` of `@velexis/testing`: it takes one of the ten synthetic Stripe webhook fixtures (`packages/testing/fixtures/stripe/`), merges the test's overrides and signs the exact payload with the endpoint's test secret as Stripe would (`Stripe-Signature`), so both backends' webhook endpoints are tested without Stripe.

A 5-minute download link to a booking document: `/v1/files/<storageKey>?exp=<unix>&sig=<base64url HMAC-SHA-256>`, signed by `signUrl` of `@velexis/crypto` with the `document-url.key` (`DOCUMENT_URL_KEY_FILE`); only the path and `exp` are signed, and the file handler checks the tenant itself. The hosted storefront gets the same-origin `/api/v1/files/…`, key callers an absolute URL on the API host; an expired or altered link answers the same `403 FORBIDDEN`, and the booking page asks for a fresh one on every Download click.

Sharing one token refresh among concurrent requests, so a rotating refresh token is never presented twice (which would trip [[refresh-token-reuse]]). The portal's middleware renews an access token that expires within 30 seconds once per refresh token (keyed by its SHA-256, outcome reused for 10 s), the OTA admin de-duplicates `console.auth.refresh` per token for 30 s (`lib/refresh-dedup.ts`), and the SDK shares one refresh per refresh-token value within a [[client-family]]. In cookie mode it also runs each refresh under the origin's Web Lock `velexis-sdk:cookie-refresh`, so the tabs of a storefront refresh one after the other.

The MVP's production design (ADR-0007): every Velexis process (seven Node.js processes), PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7.4 and Caddy run on one Ubuntu 24.04 VM (4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 160 GB SSD) without Docker, as systemd units with one system user per [[trust-zone]]. Only Caddy (80/443) and SSH (22) are reachable from outside.

The SDK's bundle budget, checked by `ota/sdk/scripts/check-size.mjs` on every build: the ESM bundle may be at most 25 KB (25 × 1024 bytes) min+gzip or the build fails; it is about 15.8 KB today. Should the console namespace ever push it past, console moves to an entry of its own.

The admin user's second factor for SSH on the VM (PCI DSS 8.4.2, ADR-0027): with `ADMIN_MFA=fido2` (the default) only FIDO2 security keys with touch and PIN (`sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com`, `verify-required`), with `ADMIN_MFA=totp` an SSH key followed by an authenticator code; never a password. `provision-vm.sh --steps ssh` applies it once the factor is enrolled, and a lockout guard refuses runs that would lock out the person running them.

"Open console": single sign-on from the portal into the OTA admin, which has no sign-in page and no staff passwords of its own. The portal mints a one-time [[portal-token]] for one OTA and its [[hand-off-page]] posts it to the OTA admin's `/sso`, which checks the Origin and exchanges it (`console.auth.signIn`) for a [[staff-session]] kept in `__Host-` cookies.

The console's audit row in `tenant_<key>.staff_actions`, written by the OTA API for every state-changing console call, every refused one and every [[audited-read]]: actor and role, target, reason, redacted before/after, outcome (`succeeded`, `failed` or `denied`), [[request-id]], IP and user agent. It answers who did what in an OTA's console.

E-mails to an OTA's staff about bookings that need a person: the templates `staff.ticketing_failed`, `staff.manual_review` and `staff.airline_card_alert`, queued in the [[outbox]] by the API and the worker. They go to `storefront_settings.ops_alert_email`, else to the OTA's active, verified owners, else to Velexis ops (`OPS_ALERT_EMAIL`), one outbox row per recipient.

Redis keys that end OTA admin staff sessions early, checked by the OTA API on every console request and refresh. `staffdeny:<familyId>` revokes one [[refresh-family]], and the epoch-millisecond cut-offs `staffdeny:acct:<accountId>` (written by the platform for 30 days on sign-out everywhere, password change or reset, MFA reset and account disable), `staffdeny:tenant:<tenantId>` (suspension) and `staffdeny:member:<staffId>` (console sign-out everywhere) refuse every family created at or before them.

One of the 14 console permissions of the OTA API (`StaffPermission`): `bookings:read|write|issue|cancel`, `customers:read`, `queues:read`, `supplier_requests:read`, `amadeus:read|write`, `settings:read|write` and `payments:read|capture|refund`. Each console operation names one in `x-permission` and the matrix in `roles.ts` grants them per [[staff-role]]; a missing one answers `403 FORBIDDEN` with `details.requiredPermission` and an audit row, and the OTA admin shows an action only when the role and the API's `permissions` allow it.

The role of a [[membership]] in one OTA (`platform.tenant_memberships.role`): `owner`, `admin`, `agent`, `finance` or `viewer`, called `TenantRole` on the platform and `StaffRole` on the OTA side. On the platform the matrix in `memberships/tenant-roles.ts` decides which portal operations each role may call (non-members get 404, other roles 403); on the OTA side `roles.ts` maps it to the console's [[staff-permission]]s and to whether the live environment may be opened.

An OTA staff member's console session in one OTA: a 15-minute EdDSA access token (`typ: staff`, with `tid`, `roles` and `sid`) and a rotating `srt_…` refresh token whose [[refresh-family]] lives at most 12 hours in Redis `staffsess:<familyId>`. It is opened by [[sso]] from the portal, kept by the OTA admin in HttpOnly `__Host-` cookies, refreshed through `console.auth.refresh` and checked on every call against the `staffdeny:*` keys and the cached membership.

The text printed after `VELEXIS*` on a traveller's card statement for an OTA in Velexis [[account-mode]], kept on its velexis-mode [[payment-connection]]: 2 to 22 characters of ASCII letters, digits and single spaces, starting with a letter or digit and containing at least one letter (a default is derived from the OTA's name, else its key). The portal previews the statement line in capitals and warns when Stripe would cut it at 22 characters.

A fresh TOTP verification that renews the session's MFA time before a sensitive action: the platform's `RecentMfaGuard` needs `mfa_at` in the access token within the last 15 minutes, else `401 REAUTH_REQUIRED`. The portal (`POST /v1/auth/step-up`) and the platform admin then ask for the code in a [[step-up-dialog]] and resend the same form; it guards for example granting owner, the payout account, live keys, [[go-live]], Amadeus credentials, settlement approval and MFA resets.

The dialog of the portal and the platform admin (`StepUpDialog`) that opens when a server action answers `stepUp: true`: it sends the authenticator code to the step-up operation (`adminStepUp` in the admin), stores the renewed session cookies and re-submits the same form data, the same reason included. Cancelling runs nothing.

The file store of `@velexis/db` for documents and uploads (`StorageAdapter`, `createStorage`): keys `tenant_<key>/…` or `platform/…`, atomic writes with mode 0600, and `signedUrl` through an injected signer. Only the `local` driver (`LocalDiskStorage`) exists. `s3` passes config validation but makes the OTA API and worker fail at start (`createStorage: the s3 storage driver is not implemented yet`).

The hosted, multi-tenant website of every OTA (`ota/frontend`, `@velexis/ota-frontend`): static HTML pages, Tailwind CSS 4 and vanilla ES modules from one Vite build that Caddy serves for all OTAs. The host name (`<key>.ota.example.com` or a verified [[custom-domain]]) picks the tenant, and every booking function is a same-origin `/api` call to the OTA API through the SDK in [[cookie-mode]].

An image uploaded in the OTA admin for the storefront (`tenant_<key>.storefront_assets`, `ast_…`) of kind `logo`, `logo_dark`, `logo_square`, `favicon`, `og_image` or `page_image`. The type is sniffed from the bytes (PNG, JPEG or WebP, ICO for a favicon, never SVG), files above 1 MB and logos above 2000 × 2000 are refused with `422 ASSET_INVALID`, and it is served publicly at `/v1/assets/<key>/<id>.<ext>`.

The shared start-up of every storefront page (`ota/frontend/src/boot.js`): it loads the [[runtime-configuration]], redirects to the [[primary-host]], applies the theme, renders header, footer and [[test-mode-banner]], restores the session and sets up the currency, and renders a full-page state when `storefront.get` fails (suspended, unknown host, outage). The isolated airline-card page does not run it.

An OTA's `test` or `live` mode (`platform.tenants.storefront_environment`): `test` until [[go-live]], then `live` for good. It decides which Amadeus and Stripe connections and which API keys the storefront uses; every supplier- or payment-bound tenant row carries `environment`, so test and live bookings never mix (a test booking answers 404 on a live storefront), while markups, fees, pages and templates are shared. The OTA admin works in either through [[x-velexis-environment]].

Automatic checks attached to every storefront end-to-end journey (`tools/e2e/support/storefront-guards.ts`): no unexpected third-party request or cookie and no serious axe accessibility violation. On the airline-card journey `card-leak-guards.ts` also fails the test when a card value appears anywhere but the completion request.

The single settings row of an OTA (`tenant_<key>.storefront_settings`, fixed id `sfs_default`): brand and colours, locales and currencies, [[ticketing-policy]], time-to-live values, airline-card switches, the Amadeus booking queue, time zone, `ops_alert_email` and features. The OTA admin saves it with `If-Match` (`412 PRECONDITION_FAILED` on a stale version); each change bumps `version` and drops the storefront caches.

The card payment provider of both products. The OTA backend takes customer payments with PaymentIntents (manual capture), refunds and signed webhooks, on Velexis's account or the OTA's own connected one; the platform bills OTA subscriptions through [[stripe-billing]] and links OTAs' own accounts with [[stripe-connect-standard]]. Locally only test mode is used, with the [[stripe-cli]] forwarding webhooks.

Velexis's own Stripe account for OTA subscriptions (M5, behind `FEATURE_STRIPE_BILLING`): Stripe Checkout to choose a plan, the Stripe [[customer-portal]] to change it, and webhooks to `/webhooks/stripe/billing` that the [[stripe-event-inbox]] stores and the platform worker applies after re-fetching the object, keeping `platform.subscriptions` and `invoices` in sync. Before it, early-access trials are run by hand as manual subscriptions.

Stripe's command-line tool, whose `stripe listen` forwards test-mode webhooks to a local backend. `tools/dev/stripe-listen.sh` runs the OTA payments and platform billing listeners (or `--only ota|billing`) and prints their signing secrets for `.env.local`; it never uses live mode, and automated tests do not need it (they sign fixtures with [[signed-stripe-event]]).

Linking an OTA's own Stripe account by OAuth ("Connect with Stripe", `connect_standard`, feature `FEATURE_OWN_STRIPE`): `startStripeConnect` stores a single-use 256-bit state in Redis `stripe:oauth:<sha256>` for 10 minutes and sends the owner to connect.stripe.com. Stripe's return to the portal's `/connect/stripe/callback` names no OTA, so the portal keeps it in the `__Host-vxp_connect` cookie; Connect account events then keep the [[payment-connection]]'s status and capabilities current.

The platform's table of received Stripe webhooks, `platform.stripe_events`: every verified billing or Connect event is stored once by its event id before processing, then handled by the platform worker, which re-fetches the object from Stripe. Its statuses are `received`, `processing`, `processed`, `ignored` and `failed`; the admin's `/stripe-events` page lists failed and ignored events first and can reprocess one ([[stripe-event-reprocess]]).

The platform admin's Reprocess action on a `failed` or `ignored` Stripe event (`adminReprocessStripeEvent`, audited as `stripe_event.reprocessed`): it puts the row back to `received`, the API answers `202` before the worker runs, and the worker re-fetches the object from Stripe and applies it again. Fix the cause first, or it fails the same way.

The OTA API's endpoints for signed Stripe events: `/webhooks/stripe/velexis/{environment}` (Velexis's account), `/webhooks/stripe/connect/{environment}` (Connect) and `/webhooks/stripe/c/{connectionId}` (an OTA's own account). Each checks `Stripe-Signature` over the exact body, stores the event as a tenant `payment_events` row and lets the worker apply it after re-reading the object from Stripe instead of trusting the body; an event for no known tenant or account is logged and acknowledged without effect.

The [[amadeus-stub]]'s in-memory flight orders (`tools/amadeus-stub/src/orders.ts`): created, issued with e-tickets, patched, cancelled, and changed by the airline when a test calls `orders.cancelByAirline` or `orders.changeSegment`. A restarted stub forgets them, cards are kept only masked, and card `4000000000000002` is declined.

A behaviour of the [[amadeus-stub]] chosen per request by the `X-Stub-Scenario` header or as the default (`setDefaultScenario`): `success`, `server-error`, `rate-limited`, `timeout`, `timeout-lost`, `sold-out`, `price-changed`, `ticketing-failed`, `version-conflict` or `cancel-refused`. Magic values select behaviour without a header for end-to-end runs, such as destination `ZZZ` for no offers.

The portal component `SubmissionStatus` that follows an Amadeus [[credential-submission]] by reading it every 2 seconds, one read at a time, until it is final, then words each outcome in plain language without showing the error code or the API's message.

An OTA's billing relation to a [[plan]] (`platform.subscriptions`, `sub_…`), billed by Stripe or managed by hand, with at most one current row per OTA (`subscriptions_current_uq`). Its status (`trialing`, `active`, `past_due`, `paused`, `canceled`, `incomplete`, `incomplete_expired`, `unpaid`) drives the trial and payment banners and, through billing sync's status rules, billing [[suspension]] and resume.

An OTA's Amadeus connection per environment (`platform.supplier_connections`, `sc_…`): `credential_source` `velexis` (the shared [[velexis-amadeus-account]] through an assigned office) or `tenant` (the OTA's own encrypted credentials), with offices, ticketing defaults, monitored queues and a status (`pending_verification`, `active`, `invalid_credentials`, `disabled`). The OTA API reads it read-only and answers `424 SUPPLIER_NOT_CONFIGURED` without an active one; platform admins can disable or re-enable it with a reason and assign an office to a waiting one.

The OTA admin's `/supplier-log` page over [[supplier-request]] rows (`tenant_<key>.supplier_requests`, permission `supplier_requests:read`): every Amadeus call with operation, status, error codes, duration and redacted bodies, searchable by the Velexis [[request-id]]. It is where to see what Amadeus actually answered.

One redacted log row per Amadeus call in `tenant_<key>.supplier_requests` (`sreq_…`): operation, API, status, outcome, duration, the request id and the request and response bodies after redaction, linked to its booking or search. The retention job deletes rows after 90 days, and the console shows them in the [[supplier-log]].

Amadeus did not answer Flight Create Orders readably (a timeout, a 5xx or an unreadable answer once the request may have reached it): the order may exist, so the API keeps the booking `pending`, sets `reconcile_until` 15 minutes ahead and answers `504 SUPPLIER_TIMEOUT` with the booking id (replayed for the same idempotency key until decided). [[reconciliation]] then looks for the order in the booking queue by its [[velexis-remark]], and the storefront opens the confirmation in pending mode and never sends the payment again.

Blocking an OTA: `active → suspended` with a `suspension_reason` of `abuse`, `request` or `admin` (by a platform admin) or `billing` (by billing sync only). Within 60 seconds the storefront, OTA API and console answer `403 TENANT_SUSPENDED` and the portal makes the OTA's forms read-only, while the `tenant.suspend` job lets the OTA worker write `staffdeny:tenant:<id>` and keep ticketing, syncing, refunding and mailing paid bookings. Resume reverses it; a billing suspension only while the subscription is `trialing` or `active`.

`pnpm db:codegen` (`packages/db/scripts/codegen.mjs`) migrates a scratch database with the repository's platform, reference and tenant files and generates the Kysely table types `PlatformDatabase`, `ReferenceDatabase` and `TenantDatabase` (e.g. `src/generated/tenant.ts`). The files are committed and never edited by hand; CI fails when they are out of date.

One OTA as a customer of Velexis: a row of `platform.tenants` (`ten_…`) with a unique [[tenant-key]], a plan, a [[storefront-environment]] and a status (`provisioning`, `active`, `suspended`, `deprovisioning`, `deleted` or `failed`), plus its own PostgreSQL [[tenant-schema]] `tenant_<key>` on the OTA side. The OTA API serves only `active` tenants and reads the row read-only through a 60-second Redis cache that [[vx-invalidate]] events clear.

The notice the portal shows above every page of one OTA (`TenantBanner`): suspended with its reason, payment failed (`past_due`), trial ending with the days left (owners and finance only) and test mode.

The deploy step that applies the tenant migrations to every [[tenant-schema]] (`migrate.js tenants`, run by [[velexis-deploy]] in a [[transient-unit]]): 4 schemas at a time, each in its own transaction under an advisory lock on the schema name, continuing past failures and failing the deploy with exit code 3 when more than 10 % of the schemas fail. With 10 % or fewer failures it exits 0 and the deploy switches anyway: the failed schemas stay on the old version until the next deploy (read `failed[]` of `migrate-<sha>.json`, also kept in `/var/log/velexis/`). Not to be confused with the worker's [[fan-out]].

An OTA's permanent short name: 3 to 30 lower-case letters and digits starting with a letter (`^[a-z][a-z0-9]{2,29}$`, `tenants_key_dns_ck`), never one of the reserved names (`admin`, `api`, `demo`, `test`, `www` and others) and never a key any tenant row has or had. It names the schema `tenant_<key>` and the sub-domain `<key>.<STOREFRONT_BASE_DOMAIN>` (`<key>.ota.example.com`); the portal's wizard checks it as it is typed (`invalid`, `reserved`, `taken`).

A numbered SQL file of the tenant set (`ota/backend/migrations/tenant/0001_baseline.sql` onward), applied to every [[tenant-schema]] by the deploy's [[tenant-fan-out]] and to a new schema at provisioning; tenant sets have no repeatable files, as grants come from default privileges. A platform admin can re-run one OTA's migrations (`adminMigrateTenant`, optionally up to a `targetVersion`) as a `migrate` provisioning job on the OTA worker; a failed migration never changes the OTA's status.

Same as [[staff-role]]. The platform's name (`TenantRole` in `platform/backend/src/memberships/tenant-roles.ts`) for a member's role in one OTA, `owner`, `admin`, `agent`, `finance` or `viewer`: the portal hides what a role may not do and the API refuses it with 403 (non-members get 404).

The PostgreSQL schema `tenant_<key>` that holds one OTA's data: 44 tables (bookings, payments, customers, settings, outbox, audit rows and more), named to match `^tenant_[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,39}$`. The OTA worker creates it as `velexis_provisioner` on `tenant.provision`, the same migrations from `ota/backend/migrations/tenant` run in every one, and only the OTA backend reaches it, as `velexis_ota_app` (DML through default privileges) inside [[tenant-tx]]; the platform never touches it.

The only way to reach tenant data: `tenantTx(db, schema, fn)` of `@velexis/db` validates the schema name, opens a transaction, runs `set_config('search_path', '<schema>, reference', true)` and a transaction-local `statement_timeout` (5 s by default, 15 s in the OTA backend's wrapper `ota/backend/src/tenancy/tenant-tx.ts`), then commits or rolls back. SQL never names a tenant schema, so a query cannot reach another OTA's rows, and the pooled connection carries no tenant afterwards.
Same as [[tenant-tx]]. `tenantTx` of `@velexis/db`, the transaction that pins `search_path` to one tenant schema (plus `reference`) for its duration; outside it the OTA role sees no tenant table.

The label of the terms of service in force (`termsVersion` in `platform/frontend/src/lib/terms.ts`, at most 32 characters; `2026-10-01` today). Sign-up sends it and the API keeps it in `platform.accounts.terms_version` with `terms_accepted_at`; the legal pages show the same label, which changes whenever the terms change in substance.

The fixed "Test mode: no real bookings or payments" banner every storefront page shows (with `noindex`) unless `storefront.get` says `environment = live`; an unknown value counts as test. It tells a tester that the storefront books against the Amadeus and Stripe test environments.

The database logins tests use (`packages/testing/src/roles.ts`): `velexis_test_admin` (local and CI only, never on the VM; CREATEDB and a member of `velexis_migrator`) creates and drops test databases, and `urlFor(role)` gives DSNs of the migrator, provisioner, platform and OTA roles with their committed development passwords (development only).

The integration-test database scheme of `@velexis/testing` (ADR-0022): Vitest's global setup migrates one template database per run, `velexis_test_tpl_<runId>` (platform and reference sets, `tenant_alpha`, `tenant_beta` and a tiny reference fixture), and every test file clones it in under a second with `createTestDatabase`, grants it again and drops it afterwards, even with connections open.

The Brand and theme section of the OTA admin's storefront settings (`theme-editor.tsx`): colours, fonts and corner radius with a live preview, checked against the storefront's own WCAG contrast rule (`ota/admin/src/lib/contrast.ts`) before saving.

`storefront_settings.ticketing_policy`, when an OTA's tickets are issued: `issue_after_payment` (the default, once the payment is captured), `issue_at_booking` (Flight Create Orders with issue=true) or `manual_review` (staff issue from the console). A failed issuance is retried until the ticketing deadline, and airline-card orders are always created with issue=true.

Whether a booking's tickets are issued (`bookings.ticketing_status`): `pending`, `in_progress`, `issued`, `partially_issued`, `failed` (retried by the issuance job until the deadline), `manual_review` or `not_applicable`. The storefront's confirmation and booking pages poll `bookings.getTicketingStatus` after each answer's `pollAfterSeconds` until it is final.

Caddy's on-demand TLS gate on the platform API, `GET http://127.0.0.1:3100/internal/tls/ask?domain=<host>` (`tlsAsk`): 200 for the sub-domain of a tenant in `provisioning`, `active` or `suspended`, or for a verified custom storefront domain of an `active` tenant whose plan allows custom domains while the `custom_domains` switch is on; 404 for anything else. Positive answers are cached in Redis `tlsask:<host>` for 60 s and refusals in an in-process LRU.

An e-mailed portal link that carries `?token=` (`/reset-password`, `/invitations/accept`). The portal middleware moves the token into a 15-minute `SameSite=Strict` cookie and answers a script-free page that refreshes to the clean URL, so the token never stays in the address bar, the history or a Referer.

The SDK session mode of third-party browser and app frontends, chosen by a publishable key: requests carry `X-Api-Key: pk_…`, `Authorization: Bearer` and `X-Booking-Token` from [[token-source]]s with `credentials: "omit"`, and the integrator decides where the tokens live. The page's origin must be listed on the key.

How an SDK client gets its `accessToken`, `refreshToken` or `bookingToken` in token and server mode (`TokenSource`): a string, or a function (possibly async) called before every request, so the token can live in the integrator's own store. `null` and `""` mean no token.

Time-based one-time password: the 6-digit code an authenticator app derives from the account's MFA secret every 30 seconds (`otplib`, SHA-1). The platform accepts the codes of the current step and the one before or after (±1), each step only once per account (`mfastep:<accountId>` in Redis blocks replays); it is the code of [[mfa]] sign-in and [[step-up]].

A one-off systemd unit that [[velexis-deploy]] starts with `systemd-run -p DynamicUser=yes` (`run_transient` in `deploy.sh`) to run the migrations and the reference-data loader. systemd itself reads the root-only `migrator.env` or `reference-loader.env`, so no app user's process ever holds those DSNs.

A group of processes that share keys and trust, run as one system user (ADR-0026): `velexis-platform` (platform API and worker), `velexis-ota` (OTA API and worker), `velexis-portal`, `velexis-platform-admin` and `velexis-ota-admin`. No zone user can read another zone's env files, keys or `/proc` entries; the shared group `velexis` only lets them read releases.

npm publishing without a stored token: the registry exchanges the GitHub Actions job's OIDC token for a short-lived publish token of a trusted publisher configured on the package, with provenance. It is planned for every `@velexis/ota-sdk` version after 1.0.0 (workflow `sdk-publish.yml`, environment `npm`); 1.0.0 itself is published once with a token, after which `NPM_TOKEN` is deleted and token publishing disallowed.

The per-pool result parsers of `@velexis/db` (`createTypeParsers`, ADR-0005): `numeric` and `int8` come back as strings, `timestamptz` as `Date`, `json` and `jsonb` parsed, set on each pool's own `types` so the global `pg.types` is never changed. Money therefore never becomes a JavaScript number and is computed with decimal.js.

The systemd hardening of every Velexis unit: `ProtectSystem=strict`, `PrivateTmp`, `PrivateDevices`, `ProtectProc=invisible`, no capabilities, a system-call filter, `InaccessiblePaths` for the other zones, `MemoryMax` and `LimitCORE=0`. CI's `deploy-files` job keeps every app unit, `velexis-alert@`, the health check, the egress refresh and the two log units at `systemd-analyze security` exposure 2.0 or lower.

The test helper `useRedis` of `@velexis/testing`: it connects each Vitest worker to its own Redis database `1 + (VITEST_POOL_ID % 15)` (1 to 15, never 0) and flushes it, so parallel test files never see each other's keys.

The root-owned mailer of the VM (`deploy/scripts/alert.sh`), used by every unit's `OnFailure=velexis-alert@%n.service` and by the health check, the backups and the log review. It sends over SMTP with TLS required (plain SMTP only to a loopback host), with subjects starting `[velexis][<ALERT_HOST_LABEL>]`.

Velexis's own shared Amadeus API credentials, one per environment (`platform.amadeus_accounts`), through which OTAs without their own credentials search and book via an office assigned from the [[office-pool]]. A platform admin enters or rotates them with a [[step-up]]; the secret is envelope-encrypted, verified by a token request and never shown again.

The reproducible Caddy binary with the web application firewall compiled in: Caddy v2.8.4 with coraza-caddy v2.0.0, Coraza v3.8.1 and the OWASP CRS v4.7.0, built with xcaddy by `deploy/caddy/build/build-caddy.sh` from `versions.env` and checked against its `CADDY_SHA256`. [[velexis-deploy]] installs it as `/usr/local/bin/caddy-velexis`, and `provision-vm.sh` (step caddy) links `/usr/bin/caddy` to it once.

The root-owned deploy command (`deploy/scripts/deploy.sh`, installed as `/usr/local/sbin/velexis-deploy`) and the only command the deploy user may run with sudo. `velexis-deploy <sha>` verifies the uploaded [[release-folder]] against its [[sha256sums]], snapshots and stages system files, runs the migrations and the [[tenant-fan-out]] in [[transient-unit]]s, switches `/srv/velexis/current`, restarts the units with health checks, rolls back automatically on failure and prunes to five releases; `--rollback` and `--status` are its other modes.

The SDK's base error class (`VelexisError`, tested with `isVelexisError`) and its 13 subclasses, chosen from the [[error-envelope]]'s status and code: `ValidationError`, `AuthenticationError`, `PermissionError`, `NotFoundError`, `ConflictError` (with `PriceChangedError` and `SoldOutError`), `ExpiredError`, `PaymentError`, `RateLimitError`, `SupplierError`, `ConnectionError` and `ServerError`. Each carries `code`, `status`, `requestId`, `details`, `fieldErrors` and `retryable`, and `toJSON()` never contains keys or tokens.

The general remark `VELEXIS <reference>` (sub-type BACKOFFICE) written into every Amadeus order Velexis creates; the order is also placed on the OTA's booking queue (`storefront_settings.booking_queue_number`, seeded 50, category 0). After a [[supplier-timeout]], [[reconciliation]] lists that queue and accepts only a PNR that carries the remark; a name match alone never counts.

`sudo velexis-run <zone> <command…>` (`deploy/scripts/run-as.sh`, installed in `/usr/local/sbin`) runs a one-off CLI command as a [[trust-zone]]'s user with the identity, env files, working directory and sandbox of that zone's installed unit. Its exit code is the command's; 125 means it refused to start (bad arguments, no unit, no release folder).

The JavaScript client of the OTA booking API (`ota/sdk`, npm `@velexis/ota-sdk`): vanilla ES2022 modules with JSDoc types and no runtime dependencies, one method per [[x-sdk-method]] (129 in 8 namespaces: account, auth, bookings, checkout, console, flights, reference, storefront). The hosted storefront uses it in [[cookie-mode]], the OTA admin in [[server-mode]] and third-party frontends in [[token-mode]]; its JSDoc types must match `docs/velexis-sdk/sdk/src/*.d.ts`.

The Redis pub/sub channel `vx:invalidate` (`INVALIDATION_CHANNEL` of `@velexis/api-types`) on which the platform publishes `{ v: 1, type, …ids }` after committing a change to a row the OTA backend caches; the types are `tenant`, `domain`, `api_key`, `connection`, `membership`, `account`, `amadeus_account` and `plan`. The OTA API's subscriber drops the matching cache keys at once, and their 60-second TTLs cover a lost message.

Same as [[coraza-waf]]. The web application firewall inside Caddy: Coraza with the OWASP Core Rule Set, blocking on the OTA API host and on the storefront's `/api/*` and `/checkout/*`, logging only elsewhere.

A narrow exception in `deploy/caddy/waf/exclusions.conf` that lets a legitimate request through the [[coraza-waf]]: one rule, one argument, one path, each with its reason. Rule 10001, for example, keeps Stripe's webhook paths (`/webhooks/stripe/…`) in detection only, because a refused event would stall a payment or refund and customer-typed text can look like an attack.

The pattern both backends use for Stripe webhooks: verify the signature, store the event once by its event id before processing (`platform.stripe_events` on the platform, `tenant_<key>.payment_events` on the OTA side), answer Stripe, then let the worker apply it after re-fetching the object from Stripe. A redelivered event changes nothing, and an event for no known tenant is logged and acknowledged.

The OpenAPI extension that names an operation's SDK method as a dotted path (`flights.search`, `console.settings.markupRules.update`); 129 operations of the OTA document carry one, and `x-sdk-exclude` operations such as the file download have none. The SDK's [[route-table]] is generated from it, and the [[parity-test]] requires the document's set to equal the client's methods exactly.

The request header (`test` or `live`) that picks the environment of a console call made with the OTA admin's [[service-key]]: required there (`400 VALIDATION_FAILED` when missing or invalid, and the permission guard checks that the role may open live), and refused with `400` from any other secret key, whose environment is the key's own. The SDK's `environment` option adds it to console operations.
